title: Concurrency, Admission & Run-Root Hygiene
description:
Purpose: how concurrent VMs and stale state are bounded.
Contract: admission-limited via semaphore; stale state reaped by background recovery loop; ambiguous state preserves residue; cross-process collision avoided by sha256-of-path.
Surface: 05-consumers Direct consumers, lifecycle.rs run-root recovery, probe.rs.
Evidence: m80/docs/behaviors/concurrency/ + m80/<crate>/tests/concurrency/.

title: Admission limiting
description:
Contract: AdmissionLimitedSandboxBackend wraps backend with a semaphore; M80_FIRECRACKER_MAX_CONCURRENT_VMS bounds concurrent VMs; admission is single-host scope; multi-host placement is the caller's concern.
Surface: 05-consumers AdmissionLimitedSandboxBackend.
Evidence: m80/docs/behaviors/concurrency/admission.md + m80/<crate>/tests/concurrency/admission.rs.

title: Gate VM creation by a tokio Semaphore wrapping the inner backend
description:
Behavior: The Firecracker backend is wrapped in an admission-limiting layer that holds an `Arc<Semaphore>` permit pool and grabs one owned permit per VM lifecycle, releasing it when the VM is torn down.
Source: predecessor `services/sandbox-executor-rs/src/lib.rs:1330-1354` (`AdmissionLimitedSandboxBackend::new` constructs `Semaphore::new(max_concurrent_vms.get())`).

title: Stale-VM detection
description:
Contract: per-VM ownership markers identify stale processes; lease files checked alongside socket reachability; vsock and API-socket reachability probed; indeterminate state preserved (only confidently-dead VMs reaped).
Surface: probe.rs.
Evidence: m80/docs/behaviors/concurrency/stale-detection.md + m80/<crate>/tests/concurrency/stale_detection.rs.

title: Identify ownership via run-dir ownership.json marker file
description:
Behavior: A run directory is considered owned by m80 only when it contains a parseable `ownership.json` marker file at the run-dir root; directories without the marker are skipped during recovery and probing.
Source: predecessor `crates/sandbox/agent-sandbox-firecracker/src/foundation.rs:39` (`RUN_OWNERSHIP_MARKER_FILE = "ownership.json"`) + `probe.rs:161-163` (`should_probe_run_dir` requires the marker).

title: Combine lease liveness, API socket, and vsock probe to classify health
description:
Behavior: A VM is classified Healthy when its lease is live AND its API socket is reachable AND a vsock probe round-trip succeeds; missing any of the three drops it to Stuck or Degraded based on the failure-triage bundle.
Source: predecessor `crates/sandbox/agent-sandbox-firecracker/src/probe.rs:165-185` (`observe_owned_run_dir`) + `270-287` (`derive_probe_health` with three signals).

title: Preserve residue on ambiguity rather than deleting on uncertainty
description:

title: Reset-evidence vocabulary in Stop events (typed exit reasons)
description:
Stop events today are scalar. We need a typed exit-reason field distinguishing the genuinely different cases.

## Reference

CLAUDE.md scope boundary excludes predecessor-style "Stage-H semantic events", but VM-lifecycle reset evidence is squarely in scope. Critical for snapshot-restore (m80-rrp.3) work — knowing whether a stop was clean lets restore decide whether to reuse state or restart.

## Scope

- Add ExitReason enum to the diagnostics.jsonl Stop event: NormalStop, ForceKill, KernelPanic, OomKill, SnapshotCapture, VmmExited(code).
- m80-firecracker classifies based on host-visible truth only (signal received, exit code observed, vsock graceful-stop ack vs SIGKILL fallback).
- No log-line scraping; no guess-from-context.
- Persisted in diagnostics.jsonl Stop event; readable by m80 inspect.

## Acceptance

- Each variant has a path in m80-firecracker that produces it (vsock graceful → NormalStop, SIGKILL after timeout → ForceKill, etc.).
- Test pins one variant per scenario.
- m80-rrp.3 (snapshot capture) emits SnapshotCapture, distinguishing it from a normal stop.

title: Per-phase timing instrumentation as first-class structured events
description:
Formalize what 577412f / cc2aed2 partly added: per-phase boot timing as typed events in diagnostics.jsonl, not just tracing spans.

## Reference

Commit cc2aed2 added per-phase timing instrumentation to launch.rs. m80-1f8.1.2 (diagnostic phases) lists StartupScavenge through Delete. Today timing lives in tracing spans only — gone after process exit.

## Scope

- Define PhaseStarted { phase, started_at } and PhaseCompleted { phase, started_at, ended_at, duration_us, outcome } event variants in the diagnostics.jsonl schema (schema_version bump or compatible additive change).
- m80-firecracker emits the events at every phase boundary already covered by tracing.
- Phases enum is shared with m80-1f8.1.2.
- Outcome is a typed enum (Ok / Err(class) / TimedOut) — no string collapse.

## Acceptance

- A successful launch produces a sequence of paired Started/Completed events covering every phase.
- A failed launch produces a Started without Completed, or Completed with outcome=Err.
- Test pins the phase count + ordering for a clean launch.
- Schema versioning documented.

title: Vsock metrics channel: guestd publishes counters/gauges over vsock (kata-style)
description:
Add a guest-side metrics channel inspired by kata's vsock-exporter pattern (src/agent/vsock-exporter). Guestd publishes typed counters and gauges over vsock; host renders them in the Prometheus scrape output.

## Reference

kata-exploration/01-architecture-and-crate-map.md mentions the vsock-exporter crate. Kata's pattern: small in-VM crate exposes a tiny ttRPC service; host calls into it during scrape. m80 equivalent: extend m80-proto with a Metrics request that returns a fixed-shape struct (CPU usage from /proc/stat, mem usage from /proc/meminfo, guestd-internal counters).

## Why

Without this, host-side metrics show only what the host can observe (cgroup totals). Guest-internal context (per-process, per-syscall classes, agent-tier counters) is invisible.

## Scope

- Add Metrics request/response to m80-proto (typed fields, no free-form key-value).
- m80-guestd implements it: read /proc/stat, /proc/meminfo, expose internal counters (requests served, errors).
- m80-observability scrape rendering includes guest-side metrics with a m80_guest_ prefix.
- Sampled at scrape time (no host-side polling between scrapes).

## Acceptance

- Scrape output includes m80_guest_cpu_*, m80_guest_mem_*, m80_guest_requests_total.
- Test: a guest under synthetic load shows non-zero CPU + memory in the scrape.

## Out of scope

- ttRPC migration (we stay JSON-framed per m80-proto).
- Aggregation across VMs (single-VM scrape only).

title: Guest-side log surface (visible guest stderr → host-readable, real time)
description:
Today the m80-1f8 epic covers HOST-side observability only (diagnostics.jsonl, probe, health, scrape). Guest-side stderr is structurally invisible until you SSH in or read logs post-mortem. The CLAUDE.md "diagnostics before hypotheses" principle (added 2026-05-04) is grounded in a real incident (ubuntu/idle 40 % flake) where one timestamped guest line would have saved an hour of investigation.

This epic closes the gap. The guest emits structured stderr; the host captures it in real time and persists per-VM; consumers (m80 logs, m80 diag) read it.

## Children

- m80-guestd structured stderr emission (boot_log lines: timestamp + phase + request_id + message)
- systemd unit StandardError=journal+console wiring + PID-1 console redirect equivalent
- Host captures /dev/console output to <run_dir>/console.log

## Why

Without this surface, every host-side timeout / hang / unexpected exit forces speculation. With it, the first move on any failure is "tail the guest console" — which CLAUDE.md says should always be the first move.

## Acceptance

- A guest panic produces a visible last-line message in <run_dir>/console.log within a bounded timeout.
- m80 logs <vm> (separate bead) tails this file.
- README of m80-guestd and m80-firecracker each document their half of the contract.

title: IMPL m80-guestd: structured stderr emission (timestamp + phase + request_id + msg)
description:
Today m80-guestd uses ad-hoc eprintln/log. Define a single boot_log line format and route every internal log through it.

## Format

[<RFC3339-timestamp>] [<phase>] [<request_id-or-boot>] <level> <message>

- phase: matches the diagnostics.jsonl phase enum (Boot, Ready, Exec, etc.).
- request_id: opaque ID from m80-cli/m80-firecracker, or "boot" pre-first-request.
- level: ERROR / WARN / INFO / DEBUG (DEBUG only when m80_DEBUG_WIRE or equivalent set).

## Why

Without structure, host-side capture (.5.3) is just text the user has to grep. With structure, m80 logs --request-id can filter cleanly.

## Scope

- m80-guestd uses tracing or a tiny custom layer; output to stderr.
- Never panic on log-format errors — log line emission must not fail the operation.
- Match the exit-on-error discipline: structured records to boot_log + exit(1), per CLAUDE.md.

## Acceptance

- Every existing eprintln/log call migrated.
- Test: parse 100 lines, all match the format.
- README of m80-guestd documents the format.

title: IMPL m80-image-build + m80-guestd: systemd StandardError=journal+console + PID-1 console wiring
description:
Make guest stderr reach a host-readable location. Two paths depending on init mode:

- systemd mode: m80-guestd.service has StandardError=journal+console (and matching StandardOutput).
- PID-1 mode (per m80-6a0q): guestd opens /dev/console for stderr at startup.

## Why

Per CLAUDE.md ubuntu-idle-flake postmortem: making the other side's stderr visible is THE first debugging move. Today neither path is wired correctly.

## Scope

- Edit crates/m80-image-build/assets/m80-guestd.service: StandardOutput=journal+console, StandardError=journal+console (note: this file is currently modified in working tree; coordinate).
- m80-guestd PID-1 entrypoint: dup2 stderr/stdout to /dev/console early.
- Document trade-off: console output competes with kernel messages — set printk levels appropriately or accept the noise.

## Acceptance

- A guestd panic produces a visible last line on the firecracker serial console output.
- Test that requires the rootfs and is gated on the existing real-KVM flag.
- m80-guestd README documents the contract for both init modes.

title: IMPL m80-firecracker: capture firecracker console output to <run_dir>/console.log
description:
Persist the guest console stream. Firecracker writes serial console to a file we provide via PUT /boot-source or PUT /machine-config (logger). Today we don't consume that output; it goes nowhere.

## Scope

- m80-firecracker configures the firecracker logger to a file at <run_dir>/console.log.
- Permissions match the rest of run_dir (jailer-owned, host-readable).
- Append mode; rotate / cap size out of scope (small VMs, short lifetimes).
- File survives VM stop; cleaned on Sandbox::delete().

## Coordinates with

- m80-1f8.5.2 (systemd/PID-1 console wiring) — guest emits to console; this captures it.
- m80-1f8.5.1 (structured stderr format) — defines what the captured lines look like.
- m80-cffo (m80 logs <vm>) — consumer.

## Acceptance

- After a successful launch, <run_dir>/console.log has at least one line matching the .5.1 format.
- After a guest panic, the panic message is in console.log.
- Test pins file existence and basic format.

title: Cosign/sigstore signature verification on registry pull path (v0.3 differentiator)
description:
When m80 ships a registry / image-distribution path (deferred v0.3 under m80-qokt or successor), require sigstore signature verification on pull. Smolvm verifies sha256 only — no signatures. Shipping signed-pull on day one is a clean trust differentiator.

## Reference

smolvm-exploration/06-registry-and-image-distribution.md (gap analysis) + 00-synthesis.md "Differentiation opportunities".

## Scope

- sigstore-rs as the verification library (mature, Rust-native, no Go dependency).
- Pull path: fetch image → fetch detached signature + Rekor entry → verify against trusted root → verify sha256 → admit.
- Fail-closed by default; an --insecure-skip-signature flag at most for local dev.
- Cover both keyless (Fulcio OIDC) and key-based signing modes; document which we recommend.

## Out of scope

- Image signing tooling (a separate "publish" path, can land later).
- Building a registry server (we use existing OCI registries; this is client-side).
- Defining the trust root's policy (separate decision).

## Acceptance

- Pull from an unsigned image fails by default with a clear error.
- Pull from a sigstore-signed image succeeds without flags.
- README documents the signing requirement and the dev-only escape hatch.
- Decision doc on keyless-vs-key-based signing.

## Why deferred

No m80-registry today; bead is a placeholder + design pin for v0.3. Defer date set to 2026-09-01.

title: Streaming exec: real chunk-by-chunk stdout/stderr, not buffered
description:
Today m80-guestd buffers stdout and stderr into 1 MiB Vec<u8> and returns one ExecResponse envelope at exit. Smolvm advertises streaming but their wire collects events into a Vec before returning (per smolvm-exploration recon doc 07).

Real streaming is an unclaimed differentiator. For agents this matters: long-running command output should arrive as it's produced, not at exit. Multi-minute builds, ongoing test runs, tail -f workloads — all of these are unusable today.

DESIGN: opt-in via ExecRequest.streaming: bool (default false → byte-identical v0.1 wire). When true, the response is a stream of ExecStdout/ExecStderr envelopes followed by a single ExecExit terminal envelope. Frames share request_id. Existing batched exec() rebuilt as a thin wrapper that buffers internally.

Cancellation: host disconnect → child.kill() on the next chunk write (write fails with EPIPE).
Backpressure: vsock socket buffer + pipe buffer cap unbounded buffering; slow host throttles child via blocking write.
No stdin streaming, no PTY, no concurrent execs, no compression, no resume.

PLAN: docs/planning/wire-features-bead-plan.md.

NON-GOALS: No stdin streaming (multi-frame stdin upload). No PTY allocation. No concurrent multi-exec on one connection. No compression. No resume across reconnects.
notes: Cross-ref m80-qokt.2.4 (persistent-VM exec cancellation contract): both epics want the same Cancel envelope on the wire. Whichever lands first owns the m80-proto Cancel-envelope type + connection.rs dispatch arm; the second epic's IMPL leaf consumes the existing envelope. If this epic lands first, m80-qokt.2.4 IMPL is reduced to host-side wiring only. See perf-roadmap-extended.md §4.

title: DESIGN: multi-frame wire shape, terminal frame, cancellation, backpressure
description:
Pin the streaming contract:
1. Opt-in: ExecRequest gains streaming: bool (default false; serde skip-if-default → byte-identical v0.1 wire when unset).
2. Frame shape: when streaming=true, response is N>=0 of Envelope<ExecStdout>+Envelope<ExecStderr> (chunks in arrival order) followed by exactly one Envelope<ExecExit>. All share the request_id of the request.
3. ExecStdout/Stderr: { request_id (echo via Envelope), bytes (base64), seq: u32 } where seq is monotonic per stream within one request.
4. ExecExit: terminal payload carrying ExecStatus + Option<exit_code> + total_stdout_bytes + total_stderr_bytes + truncated. Same shape as today's ExecResponse minus the buffered bytes.
5. Cancellation: host disconnect during streaming triggers child.kill() on the guest's next write attempt (EPIPE on writer drives detection). Document this as the cancellation contract.
6. Backpressure: capture threads (existing) write into BufWriter on the connection — when the host stalls reading, the kernel socket buffer + pipe buffer fill, the capture-thread write blocks, the child process eventually blocks on its own pipe write. No unbounded in-guest buffer.
7. Batched exec() compatibility: the existing exec() API stays, but is now built on top of exec_streaming() — buffers chunks into a Vec<u8> with the same 1 MiB cap as today.

ACCEPTANCE: doc at docs/design/wire-streaming-exec.md with frame timeline diagram, cancellation FSM, backpressure narrative. m80-proto README updated. No code.

EFFORT: S (3-4 hours).
notes: Cross-ref m80-qokt.2.4 (persistent-VM cancellation): the Cancel envelope this DESIGN locks is the SAME envelope persistent-VM cancellation needs. Lock the contract once: { request_id, sender: host|guest, reason: CallerDropped|TimedOut|Other(String) }. Both epics consume the same wire surface. See perf-roadmap-extended.md §4.

- ExecStderr { seq: u32, bytes: Vec<u8> /* base64 */ } + KIND
- ExecExit { status, exit_code, total_stdout_bytes, total_stderr_bytes, truncated, timing } + KIND
- ExecRequest gains streaming: bool with #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = is_false)] so wire is byte-identical for streaming=false consumers.

title: IMPL m80-guestd: streaming capture path
description:
In connection.rs handle_exec arm: when ExecRequest.streaming is true, replace the buffered capture_stream/Vec<u8> path with chunked emission.

Existing capture-thread shape stays: spawn one thread per pipe (stdout, stderr) reading 4 KiB at a time. Instead of pushing into a Vec, the thread writes Envelope<ExecStdout>/Envelope<ExecStderr> frames directly to the connection's BufWriter, taking a Mutex<&mut BufWriter> lock for serialization. seq increments per stream.

When child exits: drain capture threads, then write Envelope<ExecExit>.

CRITICAL: a write-failure (EPIPE on host disconnect) on any chunk frame must immediately call child.kill() and return; capture threads exit; no ExecExit frame. The connection arm returns Continue; the main accept loop continues. Document this as the cancellation behavior.

ACCEPTANCE:
- crates/m80-guestd/src/connection.rs handle_exec arm gains streaming branch.

EFFORT: M-L (2 days).

title: IMPL m80-firecracker: exec_streaming + buffered exec rebuild
description:
Add to RunningSandbox:
- exec_streaming(req: ExecRequest, on_chunk: impl FnMut(ExecChunk)) -> Result<ExecExit, FcError> where ExecChunk is enum { Stdout(seq, bytes) | Stderr(seq, bytes) }. Sends the request with streaming=true; reads frames from Channel until ExecExit; calls on_chunk for each Stdout/Stderr in order.
- exec(req: ExecRequest) -> Result<ExecResponse, FcError>: rebuild on top of exec_streaming. Buffer Vec<u8> for stdout and stderr, capped at 1 MiB each (same as today). On overflow set truncated=true. Construct an ExecResponse from buffered chunks + the ExecExit's fields.

Both methods on RunningSandbox. Existing callers of exec() see no behavior change. New callers can opt into exec_streaming.

ACCEPTANCE:

- Integration test compares exec() and exec_streaming() against the same command (echo 'a'; >&2 echo 'b'; exit 7); buffered API produces same bytes the streaming API produces concatenated; both report exit_code=7.

title: Minimal-init rootfs: skip systemd, run m80-guestd as PID 1
description:
**Cold-boot win epic.** Today user-space init (systemd → multi-user.target → ~30
deps → m80-guestd.service) dominates the ~1.8s end-to-end cold launch. Replace
that path with a minimal-init image where m80-guestd is PID 1 and serves vsock
directly. Estimated cold launch ~340ms (5x faster, ~3-5x faster than SmolVM).

This bead is **orthogonal** to readiness-probe work (m80-tv7i etc.) — that's a
host-side detection win, this is a guest-side bytes-on-the-wire-don't-happen win.
They compose.

## Strategy

PID-1 mode is **flag-gated alongside** the existing Ubuntu+systemd image, not a
replacement. v0.1 image stays as the resilient fallback while we shake out
PID-1 duties. Manifest schema gets a discriminator so callers (CLI, smoke
tests) pick which image and so preflight knows which artifacts to verify.

Once PID-1 is the default and stable, we can simplify (drop Ubuntu image,
remove the discriminator). Don't pre-build that simplification.

## Phases (rough sequence)

1. **DESIGN** — what does the manifest look like with two image kinds? What's
   the CLI surface (`m80-image-build run --kind=minimal|ubuntu`)? How does
   m80-firecracker pick boot args / drives based on manifest kind?
2. **GUESTD PID-1** — SIGCHLD reaper, mount /proc + /sys + /dev, signal
   handling that gracefully halts on shutdown (avoid kernel panic on exit),
   `setsid`. New nix dep usage. Behind a `--pid1` flag so existing
   systemd-launched binary keeps working unchanged.
2. **GUESTD WORKSPACE MOUNT** — when PID-1, do the `/dev/vdb → /workspace`
   mount via mount(2) instead of relying on the workspace.mount unit.
3. **IMAGE-BUILD MINIMAL** — produce a minimal rootfs (busybox + statically-
   linked guestd, /init symlink) alongside the existing Ubuntu image; new
   manifest discriminator. This is the largest implementation chunk.
4. **BOOT ARGS** — `init=/sbin/m80-guestd` (or wherever we land it) on the
   kernel cmdline; m80-firecracker reads from manifest.
5. **BENCH** — InstanceStart-PUT → Channel-ready P50/P95, idle and loaded
   host (`stress-ng --cpu 8`). Capture before/after for both image kinds.
6. **DOCS** — README on which image to use when; runtime-installation
   tradeoff (minimal image has no apt; caller pre-bakes Python/Node into
   the image or installs into /workspace at exec time).
7. **TESTS** — smoke-test variant for the minimal image.

## Out of scope (do separately)

- Stripped kernel build (smaller .config, faster kernel boot). Listed in
  the original spec but it's its own multi-day epic; tracked under a
  separate child if/when we get there.
- Snapshot-restore for minimal-init images. Snapshot execution is already
  v0.2; this epic is image-build + guest-side only.

## Risks (human review needed)

- PID-1 dying = kernel panic. We lose systemd's `Restart=on-failure`. A
  guestd panic that previously caused a soft reset now hard-kills the VM.
  Acceptable for v0.2 IF guestd is small and well-tested; revisit if it grows.
- Workspace runtime story changes. No apt, no systemd-tmpfiles, no nsswitch
  beyond what we statically include. Caller has to pre-bake or use
  /workspace at exec time. Document loudly.
- Two image kinds in m80-image-build adds ~30% to build code. Manifest
  schema gets a discriminator field. Tolerable; the alternative (ripping
  out Ubuntu support before PID-1 is proven) is worse.

## Acceptance (epic-level)

- Bench shows P50 cold-launch ≤ 500ms on idle host with minimal image.
- Smoke test passes against minimal image (one exec round-trip, sync,
  workspace persistence).
- Existing Ubuntu-image smoke test still passes (no regression).
- README documents both images and when to pick which.

title: DESIGN: manifest discriminator and CLI surface for minimal vs ubuntu images
description:
Pin the design before any code lands. Output: a doc + a code skeleton
(types only, no pipeline changes).

## Decisions to make

1. **Manifest discriminator**: enum field (e.g. \`image_kind: \"ubuntu\" | \"minimal\"\`)
   vs separate manifest variants. Recommend: tagged enum with #[serde(tag = \"image_kind\")].
   The minimal variant has no \`service_unit_path\`/\`workspace_mount_path\`/\`source_rootfs_image\`
   fields — they don't exist for that build.
2. **CLI surface**: \`m80-image-build run --config <toml>\` adds a \`[image]\` table
   with \`kind = \"ubuntu\" | \"minimal\"\`, OR a new subcommand \`build-minimal\`. Recommend:
   TOML field; same subcommand handles both via a match in pipeline.
3. **Init binary path**: \`/init\` symlink → \`/sbin/m80-guestd\` vs direct \`/init\`.
   Recommend: \`/init\` symlink; clearer for archaeology.
4. **m80-firecracker dispatch**: Sandbox::launch reads manifest.image_kind,
   picks boot_args (init= for minimal vs default for ubuntu). Encapsulate
   in a small fn; don't sprinkle match arms across phase_11.
5. **Backwards compat**: existing \`v0.1\` manifests with no \`image_kind\` field
   should be rejected (deny_unknown_fields is on; bumping schema_version to 2
   for the discriminator is the cleanest signal). Decide: bump to 2, or add
   the field with a default-on-deserialize for kind=\"ubuntu\"?

## Acceptance

- Doc at \`docs/design/minimal-init.md\` covering all 5 decisions with the
  picked option + 1-line rationale per decision.
- m80-image-manifest skeleton change: enum \`ImageKind\` + tagged manifest enum;
  \`Manifest::verify\` matches on kind to know which artifacts to hash.
- No pipeline.rs changes yet (that's the next bead).

## Effort

~half a day. Mostly thinking + doc + minor types churn.

Locks: (a) ImageKind enum + Manifest schema bump 1→2 with kind-conditional Optional<> systemd fields; (b) RootfsConfig.kind in image-build TOML; (c) boot_args_for(kind, override) dispatch in launch.rs; (d) inheritance map for .2/.3/.4/.5 IMPL leaves. No code changes — design only.

title: IMPL: m80-guestd PID-1 mode (SIGCHLD reaper, mount pseudo-fs, signal handling)
description:
Make guestd survive being PID 1. Behind a flag (\`--pid1\` or env
\`M80_GUESTD_PID1=1\`) so the existing systemd-launched binary keeps working
unchanged for the v0.1 image.

## What PID-1 has to do

1. **SIGCHLD reaper**: any orphaned process re-parents to PID 1; if PID 1
   doesn't waitpid() them they become zombies forever. Install a SIGCHLD
   handler (or signalfd loop) that drains \`waitpid(-1, ..., WNOHANG)\` until
   it returns 0/-1.
2. **Pseudo-fs mounts**: in PID-1 mode, mount \`/proc\`, \`/sys\`, \`/dev\` (devtmpfs
   is usually auto-mounted by the kernel given CONFIG_DEVTMPFS_MOUNT, but
   verify on our kernel build), and \`/dev/pts\`. Idempotent: skip if already
   mounted.
3. **Signal handling**: SIGTERM/SIGINT should clean-shutdown — flush logs,
   sync, then \`reboot(LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_POWER_OFF)\`. PID 1 dying with the
   default disposition kernel-panics; we have to handle it explicitly.
4. **setsid**: become a session/process-group leader so child processes
   don't inherit a controlling terminal weirdness.
5. **Don't crash**: any \`unwrap()\` in startup is a kernel panic. Audit
   every \`?\` in the startup path for \"is this fatal-OK or do we want to
   log-and-continue?\"

## Implementation notes

- Add \`nix\` to m80-guestd workspace deps (mount, signal, wait, reboot).
- New module \`m80-guestd/src/pid1.rs\` ~150 LOC; main.rs branches on flag.
- Existing connection.rs is unchanged — connection handler doesn't care
  whether it's PID 1 or PID N.
- The existing exec_request already does waitpid via \`child.wait()\`. The
  SIGCHLD reaper handles processes orphaned BY guestd's children (e.g. a
  bash exec that backgrounds a subprocess that outlives the request).

## Acceptance

- \`m80-guestd --pid1\` runs without crashing when launched as PID 1 (test
  via a unit test that fork+execs guestd in a new pid namespace, sends a
  child signal, asserts no zombies).
- Without \`--pid1\` flag, behavior is byte-identical to today (existing
  guestd integration tests still pass).
- Tests under \`m80-guestd/tests/pid1/\`.

## Effort

~1 day. Reaping + mount(2) is well-trodden; the panic-avoidance audit is
the slow part.
notes: src/pid_one.rs added with: is_pid_one(), enter_pid_one_mode() — installs panic hook, mounts /proc, /sys, /dev (devtmpfs); reap_pending() called from request loop after each connection. **Diverged from bead spec on signals**: no SIGCHLD/SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers — workspace lint forbids unsafe (sigaction is unsafe FFI), and host stops VM via SIGKILL on the outside, so graceful SIGTERM is moot. Orphan reap done via poll between requests; sufficient for v0.1's sequential request model. README Lifecycle section updated. cargo test/clippy clean.

title: IMPL: m80-guestd workspace mount via mount(2) when PID-1
description:
The Ubuntu image relies on the workspace.mount systemd unit to mount
\`/dev/vdb\` at \`/workspace\`. In PID-1 mode there's no systemd; guestd does
the mount itself.

## Implementation

- In PID-1 startup (after pseudo-fs mounts, before vsock bind), call
  \`mount(\"/dev/vdb\", \"/workspace\", \"ext4\", 0, NULL)\` via nix.
- Handle the \"no scratch drive provided\" case: when the host hasn't put a
  drive at \`/dev/vdb\` (no SandboxConfig.workspace), the device file won't
  exist. Skip the mount silently — connection.rs already handles
  \"\$cwd doesn't exist\" via Command spawn errors.
- mkdir -p \`/workspace\` first. \"Silent recovery\" rule (CLAUDE.md) doesn't
  apply here — the mountpoint is part of guestd's own setup, not someone
  else's invariant.
- Don't try to grow this into a generic \"mount whatever the host put on
  vdb\" abstraction. Wired path: ext4, /dev/vdb, /workspace. That's it.

## Acceptance

- PID-1-mode guestd mounts /workspace from /dev/vdb when the device exists.
- Skips silently when /dev/vdb is absent.
- Workspace persistence test (write file in VM A, read in VM B sharing the
  same scratch image) passes against minimal image.

## Effort

~half a day. Mostly verifying behavior matches the systemd unit.

## Dependency

Blocks on m80-6a0q.2 (PID-1 mode skeleton). Lands in the same module
(\`pid1.rs\`).
notes: Update 2026-05-04 (post-storage-pivot): The constants in this bead referenced /dev/vdb as the workspace device. After m80-ovrl, the drive layout is vda=base RO, vdb=overlay RW, vdc=workspace RW. The workspace mount must move from /dev/vdb to /dev/vdc, and it must occur inside the pivoted root (after pivot_root, not before). Follow-up leaf m80-ovrl.4a captures this update.

title: IMPL: minimal initramfs/rootfs in m80-image-build (busybox + static guestd + /init)
description:
Largest implementation chunk. Marked **epic** because it has its own
sub-decisions (initramfs vs initrd-less direct-rootfs; busybox vs nothing;
static guestd build mode).

## Output

A second image kind that m80-image-build produces:

- Kernel (same vmlinux as Ubuntu image — kernel-config work is a separate
  epic outside m80-6a0q's scope).
- Tiny rootfs (~10-30 MiB target) containing:
  - \`/sbin/m80-guestd\` (statically-linked or musl-linked so it doesn't need
    glibc dynamic loader from a base image)
  - \`/init -> /sbin/m80-guestd\` symlink
  - \`/lib\` with whatever guestd dlopens (probably nothing if static)
  - busybox at \`/bin/busybox\` + symlinks for \`sh\`, \`mount\`, \`umount\`, \`ls\`,
    \`cat\` (callers that exec \`bash -c\` need *something* to find at \`/bin/sh\`)
  - \`/etc/passwd\` with at minimum a root entry
  - empty \`/proc\`, \`/sys\`, \`/dev\`, \`/workspace\` mountpoints
- Manifest entry for the new kind.

## Sub-decisions (resolve early)

1. **Static vs dynamic guestd**: static (\`-C target-feature=+crt-static\` or
   musl target) is simpler — no /lib to populate. Cost: rebuild on every
   change, ~5x bigger binary. Recommend: static for now.
2. **Initramfs vs ext4**: an initramfs (cpio.gz baked into the kernel or
   loaded as initrd) eliminates the rootfs drive PUT entirely — fewer
   Firecracker REST round-trips at launch. But our existing storage prep
   logic assumes a rootfs drive. Recommend: keep ext4 rootfs for v0.2 to
   minimize launch-pipeline churn; revisit initramfs as a later perf win.
3. **Busybox**: pull from a known-good Alpine-like source, or skip and
   ship just guestd? If callers always provide \`program\`/\`args\` directly
   and never depend on \`/bin/sh\`, we can skip busybox. Recommend: include
   busybox-static; it's ~1 MiB and unblocks \`bash -c\` style callers.
4. **Sub-bead split** (decide during design, m80-6a0q.1):
   - 4a. minimal-rootfs assembly pipeline (download/copy busybox, install
        guestd, write /etc/passwd, create mountpoints, mkfs.ext4)
   - 4b. manifest writer for ImageKind::Minimal
   - 4c. Manifest::verify branch for minimal kind

## Acceptance

- \`m80-image-build run --config minimal.toml\` produces:
  - vmlinux, output.ext4 (~30 MiB), output.ext4.manifest.json
  - Manifest passes \`m80-image-build verify\`
- Loop-mounting output.ext4 shows /init -> /sbin/m80-guestd, busybox
  installed, /workspace dir present.

## Effort

~2-3 days as an epic. Could be 1 day if we accept skipping busybox and
the design bead landed clean.

## Dependency

Blocks on m80-6a0q.1 (DESIGN). Drives m80-6a0q.5 (boot args) and
m80-6a0q.7 (smoke test).
notes: Update 2026-05-04 (post-storage-pivot): The minimal-init image produced by this bead becomes the default carrier of the overlayfs+pivot setup added by m80-ovrl.4. No change to the image-build artifacts themselves is required by the storage pivot — the rootfs that m80-image-build produces still becomes /dev/vda in the guest, which is now mounted read-only as the lowerdir rather than directly as /. Kernel config gains an explicit verification of CONFIG_OVERLAY_FS=y under m80-ovrl.5; this beads captured doc/test stay correct.

title: IMPL: replace stat-poll with inotify watch + TOCTOU stat
description:
Modify `phase_12b_ready_probe` in `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs` (or, if cleaner, lift the wait into a small helper inside m80-vsock that takes `(chroot_dir, companion_name, deadline)`) to:

1. Call `Inotify::init()` and `add_watch(chroot_dir, WatchMask::CREATE)`.
2. **Immediately** stat `chroot_dir/companion_name`. If it exists, skip the read loop. (Closes the TOCTOU between guestd's bind() and our add_watch.)
3. Otherwise loop on `read_events_blocking_with_timeout(&mut buf, deadline_remaining)` until an event with `name == companion_name` arrives or the deadline expires.
4. On match, run the existing one-shot `Channel::open_uds_only(vsock_uds, GUEST_PORT_DEFAULT)` handshake.

## Companion path

Per m80-tv7i: when guestd does `VsockListener::bind((VMADDR_CID_ANY, 9001))`, Firecracker creates host-side `<vsock_uds>_9001` inside the chroot. So `chroot_dir = vsock_uds.parent()`, `companion_name = format!("{}_{port}", vsock_uds.file_name())`.

## Constraints (CLAUDE.md "What we don't want")

- One function, two phases, fallback inline. No `trait ReadyProbe` / no `ProbeStrategy` enum.
- No silent recovery — if both inotify and the fallback fail, surface the error.
- The fallback path is implemented in the FALLBACK leaf, but call sites live here.

## Acceptance

- `phase_12b_ready_probe` no longer sleeps in a polling loop on the happy path.
- TOCTOU stat is present and documented with a comment naming the race.
- Existing smoke test still passes (UDS handshake unchanged).
- Updated m80-vsock and/or m80-firecracker README 'readiness contract' section if surface changes.

## Non-goals

- Bench numbers (separate leaf).
- Removing m80-tv7i's stat-poll code (it's the fallback).

title: FALLBACK: stat-poll path when inotify init fails (EMFILE / unsupported fs)
description:
When `Inotify::init()` or `add_watch()` returns an error, fall back to m80-tv7i's stat-poll loop **inline** in the same function. Cases we care about:

- **EMFILE** — process inotify watch limit hit. Rare in our single-VM-per-process world but trivial to graceful-degrade.
- **ENOSPC** — system-wide inotify watch limit (`/proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_watches`).
- **Filesystem doesn't support inotify** — overlayfs in some container layouts, fuse mounts. We don't expect this on the run_root, but a guest jail in unusual host configs could hit it.

## Shape (inline, not an abstraction)

```rust
fn wait_for_companion(chroot: &Path, name: &str, deadline: Instant) -> Result<(), VsockError> {
    match Inotify::init() {
        Ok(inotify) => match inotify.add_watch(chroot, WatchMask::CREATE) {
            Ok(_) => return wait_via_inotify(inotify, chroot, name, deadline),
            Err(e) => tracing::debug!(err = %e, "inotify add_watch failed; falling back to stat poll"),
        },
        Err(e) => tracing::debug!(err = %e, "inotify init failed; falling back to stat poll"),
    }
    wait_via_stat_poll(chroot, name, deadline) // m80-tv7i's loop
}
```

## Acceptance

- The inotify-init failure path logs at `debug` (not `error` — graceful degrade is expected, not exceptional) with the underlying errno.
- The TOCTOU stat in the inotify path AND the polling stat in the fallback path both check the same companion filename — extract a single `fn companion_path(vsock_uds, port)` if the formula is repeated, but no further indirection.
- Test: synthesize an Inotify::init failure (or stub the call) and verify the fallback path reaches the file.

## Non-goals

- Counter/metric for how often the fallback fires (m80-observability is empty in v0.1).
- Retrying inotify init after a delay — single attempt, then poll.

title: TEST: TOCTOU stat catches file appearing between add_watch and first read
description:
Unit test for the inotify-with-TOCTOU-stat semantics, using a tempdir as a stand-in for the chroot.

## Scenarios (each its own `#[test]` per CLAUDE.md)

1. **happy path**: spawn a thread that creates `<dir>/companion` ~50 ms after the wait starts. Verify the wait returns Ok within a few ms of the create. Asserts inotify event delivery works end-to-end.
2. **TOCTOU race**: create `<dir>/companion` *before* calling the wait helper. Verify it returns Ok via the stat-after-add_watch branch — does NOT block until timeout. **This is the regression test for the race the bead is named after.**
3. **timeout**: never create the file. Verify wait returns the deadline-expired error within deadline + small slop (e.g., < 100 ms).
4. **wrong filename**: create `<dir>/other` while waiting for `<dir>/companion`. Verify wait does NOT return early; it sees a CREATE event but filters by name correctly.

## Constraints

- No tamper-and-restore; each test gets a fresh tempdir.
- No bundling failure scenarios; each scenario is its own `#[test]`.
- Tests live in m80-vsock if the helper is there, or m80-firecracker if the function stays in launch.rs. Pick one and keep tests next to the code per CLAUDE.md.

## Non-goals

- Testing the full vsock handshake (covered by smoke).
- Testing inotify init failure (FALLBACK leaf owns that).

title: BENCH: ready-latency p50/p95 vs m80-tv7i baseline
description:
Measure host-side wakeup latency from `InstanceStart` REST PUT to `Channel::open_uds_only` returning Ok. Compare:

- **A**: m80-tv7i baseline (10 ms stat-poll).
- **B**: m80-6gv9 (inotify + TOCTOU stat).

Run each ≥100 iterations on an idle host. Report p50, p95, max. Honest framing required: the floor is guest boot time + Firecracker boot + initramfs + guestd startup. We expect:

- p50 delta on order of a few ms (poll-interval-bound, m80-tv7i is already cheap on idle).
- p95 delta clearer when host is loaded (inotify wakes on kernel notify; stat-poll waits up to 10 ms per cycle and starves under load).

## Stacking

Note in the report: this latency improvement is **marginal** vs m80-tv7i alone unless stacked with **m80-6a0q** (minimal-init), which collapses the guest-boot floor. The bigger win is CPU: zero work between events vs ~1 µs/probe at 100 Hz.

## Loaded-host scenario

If feasible, run a loaded variant: `stress-ng --cpu $(nproc) --timeout 30s` in the background and re-measure. The win should be larger here because the polling thread loses its slice while the kernel-driven inotify path doesn't.

## Acceptance

- Bench is reproducible (script committed under `benches/` or `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/`).
- Numbers in the closing notes of the bead, with hardware/kernel context.
- No regression vs m80-tv7i. If inotify is somehow slower (it shouldn't be), surface the surprise; don't bury it.

## Non-goals

- Microbenchmark of inotify alone (covered upstream).
- Measuring guest-boot latency (separate concern, m80-6a0q's territory).

With m80-7tpy as the primary readiness path, inotify is largely subsumed: UnixListener::accept() already blocks event-driven on fd readiness. See docs/verifications/m80-tv7i.1-vsock-companion-file.md.

title: DX v0.2: first-touch parity with smolvm (~30s to first VM)
description:
Smolvm first-touch is ~30s (curl|bash → working VM); m80 is ~30 min. Most of the gap is missing prebuilts + README-as-contributor-doc. This epic bundles the three changes that close it.

## Children

- README rewrite as user landing page (currently reads as contributor doc)
- examples/ directory with 3 minimal artifacts (smallest plausible m80 launch invocations)
- GitHub Releases workflow publishing prebuilt kernel + rootfs + manifest tarballs

## Why

From smolvm-exploration/10-dx-docs-configuration-onboarding.md and 00-synthesis.md: smolvm's .github/workflows/release.yml is ~320 lines; m80 has zero release automation. Their README is a user landing page; ours is a contributor doc. They have an examples/ dir; we don't.

No single piece moves the needle; the trio together does. Also gates the m80-cli --quickstart bead, which assumes prebuilts exist.

## Acceptance

- Three child beads closed.
- A new contributor following only the new README + a release tarball can run a VM end-to-end without cloning the repo.

title: DOCS: rewrite README as user landing page
description:
Today's README reads as a contributor doc (workspace shape, dossier pointers, CLAUDE.md scope). A first-time visitor cannot answer "what is m80, how do I use it, what does the smallest example look like" from above the fold.

## Reference

Smolvm's README leads with a one-line value-prop, a copy-pasteable install, and a copy-pasteable first command. Source: smolvm-exploration/10-dx-docs-configuration-onboarding.md.

## Scope

- Top fold: one-sentence value prop, install line, smallest working command, expected output.
- Move contributor / dossier / scope content below the fold or to CONTRIBUTING.md.
- Keep CLAUDE.md scope split visible but not above the fold.

## Acceptance

- README's first 40 lines tell a new user what m80 is and how to run it.
- The smallest working command in the README actually works against a release tarball (depends on the prebuilt-tarballs sibling bead).

title: DOCS: examples/ directory with 3 minimal artifacts
description:
Smolvm has examples/ with runnable artifacts; m80 has none. A new user wanting to see "what does the smallest invocation look like" today has to read crate READMEs.

## Scope

Three examples, smallest each can be:

1. echo-hello: m80 launch -- echo hello (single-shot, no workspace, no network)
2. workspace-roundtrip: launch with a workspace dir, write a file, read it back on the host
3. network-egress: launch with NetworkPolicy::OutboundNat (or the v0.2 equivalent) and curl one allowed host

Each example is its own subdirectory with a README.md, a tiny shell script (or Rust main), and the exact expected output.

## Acceptance

- examples/{echo-hello,workspace-roundtrip,network-egress}/ exist with runnable artifacts.
- Each example's README points back to the relevant crate doc for depth.
- A CI job (or quickstart bead) exercises at least the echo-hello example.

title: INFRA: GitHub Releases workflow for prebuilt kernel + rootfs + manifest tarballs
description:
Smolvm publishes kernel + rootfs + manifest as a release asset; their .github/workflows/release.yml is ~320 lines. m80 has zero release automation, so first-touch requires running m80-image-build locally (~30 min cold).

## Reference

smolvm-exploration/10-dx-docs-configuration-onboarding.md and 06-registry-and-image-distribution.md.

## Scope

- GitHub Actions workflow triggered on tag push (e.g. v0.2.0).
- Runs m80-image-build to produce kernel, rootfs.ext4, image-manifest.json, m80-guestd binary.
- Uploads them as a single release asset (tarball or individual files) with sha256s.
- Workflow itself is reproducible enough that a fork can re-run it without secrets.

## Out of scope

- A registry (deferred to v0.3, see m80-qokt + cosign bead).
- Auto-publishing m80-cli binaries (separate concern).
- Any signing / attestation (sigstore bead is separate).

## Acceptance

- A GitHub Release for v0.2.x carries the artifacts.
- The README's install path can curl them.
- Quickstart bead (m80-cli --quickstart) consumes them.

title: File-ops verbs on guest wire (read/write/list/stat/chunked write)
description:
Today every 'read a file out of the VM' or 'drop a file into the VM' round-trips through bash -c with base64-encoded stdin/stdout. Expensive (process spawn + pipe), bounded by 1 MiB CAPTURE_LIMIT in connection.rs, forces shell-quoted command lines.

m80-fops adds first-class file-ops verbs to the wire — FileRead, FileWrite, FileList, FileStat, FileRemove — plus chunked-upload trio (FileWriteBegin/Chunk/Commit) for large files. The verbs run in m80-guestd directly: open path, read/write bytes, return them. No subprocess, no shell.

Why: m80's primary consumer is agent harnesses, and agents constantly move small files in and out. Smolvm's protocol shipped equivalents (smolvm-protocol/src/lib.rs); the gap is real.

Why now: wire protocol stabilised behind Envelope::kind peek-and-dispatch (already used for ShutdownRequest in m80-guestd connection.rs:73). Each new verb is a Payload impl plus a handler arm — no framing changes, no version bump, no migration story.

PLAN: docs/planning/wire-features-bead-plan.md.

NON-GOALS: No path-prefix policy (caller decides paths; layer policy in adapter). No symlink-following on read (O_NOFOLLOW final component, reject). No permissions/chown verbs (use ExecRequest). No streaming reads (FileRead returns whole body subject to max_bytes). No directory-tree creation (parent dir must exist). No checksumming on the wire (JSON+base64 framing already end-to-end checked).

title: DESIGN: file-ops verb set, error model, chunked upload protocol
description:
Pin the contract every IMPL leaf consumes:

1. Verb set: FileRead, FileWrite, FileList, FileStat, FileRemove + chunked trio FileWriteBegin/Chunk/Commit. No FileMove/FileCopy in v0.2.
2. Error model: each verb returns response with Option<FileError> discriminant (NotFound, PermissionDenied, IsADirectory, NotADirectory, SymlinkRejected, TooLarge, Io). Per CLAUDE.md no catch-and-rewrap; Io reserved for unmappable cases.
3. Symlinks: final component O_NOFOLLOW, reject as SymlinkRejected. Intermediate components follow kernel default.
4. Size caps: FileRead honours max_bytes (default FILE_READ_LIMIT = 16 MiB). FileWrite implicit cap = 64 MiB envelope; larger uploads must use chunked path.
5. Chunked state machine: Begin returns upload_id; per-connection map tracks open file handle for <path>.m80-upload.<upload_id>; Commit fsyncs+rename. Disconnect drops handle + unlinks temp. No resume across reconnects.
6. Listing: one directory level only (no recursion). DirEntry { name, kind, size }.
7. Stat: kind, size, mtime_unix_ms, mode (Unix mode as u32). No inode/device/ctime/xattrs.
8. Concurrency: each request inline on connection thread.

ACCEPTANCE: doc at docs/design/wire-fops.md with verb table, error matrix, chunked-upload sequence. m80-proto README updated. No code.

EFFORT: S (3-4 hours).

title: IMPL m80-proto: file-ops payload types and Payload impls
description:
Add 13 new payload types + Payload::KIND constants to m80-proto/src/types.rs. Re-export from lib.rs. No framing changes.

Types (full snippets in docs/planning/wire-features-bead-plan.md):
- FileReadRequest/Response with truncated flag and Option<FileError>
- FileWriteRequest/Response with mode + bytes_written
- FileListRequest/Response with Vec<DirEntry>
- FileStatRequest/Response with FileStat { kind, size, mtime_unix_ms, mode }
- FileRemoveRequest/Response
- FileWriteBeginRequest/Response with upload_id
- FileWriteChunkRequest/Response (one ack per chunk)
- FileWriteCommitRequest/Response with bytes_written total
- FileError enum, FileKind enum, DirEntry struct, FileStat struct
- FILE_READ_LIMIT_DEFAULT const

ACCEPTANCE: types.rs gains all 13 + FileError + helpers; lib.rs re-exports; round-trip tests in m80-proto/tests confirm serde + truncated + error variants survive write+read frame cycle. types.rs may exceed 500 LOC — split into types/{exec.rs, shutdown.rs, fileops.rs} per CLAUDE.md.

EFFORT: M (1 day).

title: IMPL m80-guestd: handler arms + per-connection upload table
description:
Extend connection.rs handler dispatch (already peeks Envelope<serde_json::Value>::kind for shutdown vs exec) to dispatch the 8 new verbs. Each verb arm is a small fn that opens path, reads/writes bytes, builds response.

Per-connection upload table: HashMap<UploadId, File>. Lives in connection scope (per-handle stack), not global. Drop-on-disconnect ensures temp files cleaned. Uses tempfile pattern <path>.m80-upload.<upload_id>; commit does fsync + rename.

ACCEPTANCE:
- crates/m80-guestd/src/connection.rs: 8 new arms + helper module crates/m80-guestd/src/fileops.rs.
- File-size: connection.rs may exceed 500 LOC — split into connection/{handler.rs, exec.rs, fileops.rs}.
- Tests at crates/m80-guestd/tests/fileops_*.rs covering happy + error paths per verb (one #[test] per scenario per CLAUDE.md).
- O_NOFOLLOW on final component verified with a symlink fixture.

DEPS: m80-fops.2.

EFFORT: M (1.5 days).

title: IMPL m80-firecracker: host-side wrapper API on RunningSandbox
description:
Expose ergonomic host-side wrappers on RunningSandbox so callers don't construct envelopes directly:
- read_file(path, max_bytes) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, bool /* truncated */), FcError>
- write_file(path, bytes, mode) -> Result<u64, FcError>
- list_dir(path) -> Result<Vec<DirEntry>, FcError>
- stat_file(path) -> Result<FileStat, FcError>
- remove_file(path) -> Result<(), FcError>
- upload_file_chunked(path, mode, reader, chunk_size) -> Result<u64, FcError>

Each wraps Channel send/recv with envelope construction. Map FileError to FcError variants (or carry as FcError::FileOp(FileError)). The streaming chunked uploader uses the new Begin/Chunk/Commit envelope sequence with explicit upload_id from the first response.

ACCEPTANCE:
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs (or new crates/m80-firecracker/src/fileops.rs): all 6 methods on RunningSandbox.
- Integration test exercises one full FileWriteBegin→Chunk×3→Commit upload of a 5 MiB blob; reads back via FileRead with max_bytes; asserts byte-identity.
- README m80-firecracker public-surface section updated.

DEPS: m80-fops.3.

EFFORT: M (1 day).

title: TESTS: wire round-trips, error matrix, chunked-upload edge cases
description:
Three test layers:
1. m80-proto: per-payload serde round-trip tests (already part of m80-fops.2).
2. m80-guestd unit (cfg test, no real syscalls): handler arms with mocked filesystem, asserting error mapping + chunked state-machine transitions.
3. Integration (real KVM, root, #[ignore]): launch a VM via existing test harness; exercise each verb against a tmpfs-backed /workspace; specifically:
   - FileRead happy + max_bytes truncation
   - FileWrite happy + mode bits + parent-dir-missing error
   - FileWriteChunked: small + 5 MiB blob; mid-upload disconnect (must clean temp file)
   - Concurrent uploads on one connection (multiple upload_ids in flight)
   - FileList of /etc with at least one symlink — verify SymlinkRejected on FileRead but symlink kind in DirEntry
   - FileStat: ctime not present, mtime within 5 s of write
   - FileRemove on missing → NotFound; FileRemove on directory → IsADirectory
ACCEPTANCE: cargo test for m80-proto + m80-guestd unit clean; sudo -E cargo test -- --ignored for integration green.

DEPS: m80-fops.3, m80-fops.4.

EFFORT: M (1 day).

title: DOCS: behavior captures + adapter migration note
description:
Land doc diffs:
1. crates/m80-proto/README.md — verb list, error model, chunked-upload diagram. The README's 'Public surface' section gains the new types.
2. crates/m80-guestd/README.md — handler dispatch table; behavior captures at docs/behaviors/wire-protocol/{file-read,file-write,file-list,file-stat,file-remove,chunked-upload}.md.

title: Inverted readiness: guest connects out to host instead of host polling
description:
Event-driven readiness via inverted vsock: m80-guestd connects OUT to
the host on a known port at startup; the host listens on
`<vsock_uds>_<ready_port>` and `accept()`s. Zero polling, zero
firecracker file-naming dependency.

## Status: PRIMARY readiness path post-tv7i refutation

The sibling bead m80-tv7i was closed `--reason "premise-refuted"` on
2026-05-04. Source-code reading of firecracker
(`/tank/projects/firecracker/src/vmm/src/devices/virtio/vsock/unix/muxer.rs:619-641`)
showed that `<vsock_uds>_<port>` is host-pre-created and Firecracker
**connects()** to it when the guest initiates outbound — the exact
mechanism this bead relies on. So m80-7tpy's design is now
*confirmed by source code* to work, while m80-tv7i's was
*refuted by source code*. See
`docs/verifications/m80-tv7i.1-vsock-companion-file.md`.

m80-bgas remains the parity backstop. m80-6gv9 (inotify) is no longer
relevant as a stack-on-top for m80-tv7i; if pursued, it would watch
for the `accept()`-completion event via epoll/io_uring, but
`UnixListener::accept()` already blocks event-driven on the underlying
fd readiness, so m80-6gv9 is largely subsumed by m80-7tpy.

## Design (source-code-validated)

- Host (m80-firecracker `phase_12b_ready_probe` replacement): pre-create
  `<jail>/vsock.sock_<READY_PORT>` as a `UnixListener` BEFORE
  `InstanceStart`. Block on `listener.accept()` with a deadline.
- Guest (m80-guestd at startup): bind exec listener on port 9001 (existing),
  then open an outbound vsock connection to `(VMADDR_CID_HOST=2, READY_PORT)`
  and write one byte: `m80_proto::PROTOCOL_VERSION as u8`.
- Host: `accept()` returns the moment guestd connects. Read 1 byte;
  compare against `PROTOCOL_VERSION`. Mismatch → typed
  `VsockError::ProtocolVersionMismatch`.

## Why this works (cited)

- `firecracker/src/vmm/src/devices/virtio/vsock/unix/muxer.rs:99-104`
  — `host_sock_path` doc-comment: "Unix sockets listening on specific
  ports. I.e. `<this path>_<port number>`".
- `firecracker/src/vmm/src/devices/virtio/vsock/unix/muxer.rs:619-641`
  — `handle_peer_request_pkt` does `UnixStream::connect(port_path)`
  on guest-initiated outbound. The host is the `UnixListener` side.
- Bonus: the byte-payload carries proto-version, so we get a
  protocol-mismatch check at first contact for free.

## Acceptance

- VERIFY: live KVM run shows `<jail>/vsock.sock_<READY_PORT>` exists
  before InstanceStart and `accept()` returns immediately when guestd
  is up. Write a small fixture in `m80-firecracker/tests/`.
- IMPL host: pre-bind the ready listener in `phase_4_jailer_materialize`
  or just before `phase_12a_instance_start`. Move readiness probe
  from `phase_12b_ready_probe` to `accept_with_deadline`.
- IMPL guestd: `vsock::VsockStream::connect(VMADDR_CID_HOST, READY_PORT)`
  in `m80-guestd/src/main.rs::run` after the exec listener is bound.
- BENCH: P50/P95 of `InstanceStart REST PUT → accept() returns`. Target:
  <50ms on idle host (bound below by guest kernel boot).
- DOCS: m80-vsock and m80-firecracker READMEs updated for the new
  contract.

## Open question

`READY_PORT` constant: pick a value that won't conflict with v0.2
agent ports. Suggestion: 9000 (one below the existing exec port 9001),
defined in `m80-proto::version`.
notes: Inverted readiness fully implemented + validated. N=20 ubuntu/idle = 20/20 pass (was 50-60% pre-fix). Note: the ubuntu/idle 40% flake had TWO causes — (a) the polled-CONNECT/OK race that this bead's design eliminated, AND (b) a systemd ordering issue (m80-guestd.service depended on multi-user.target which pulled in network-wait-online's bimodal 90s timeout, plus an ordering cycle). Both fixed in ad00c02. .1 VERIFY narrowed to 'n/a — design proven correct in production'; .2 DESIGN was lock-in per the bead description; .5 BENCH-vs-bgas was made obsolete by m80-bgas's polling being removed entirely.
close_reason: implemented (ad00c02); 100% pass at N=20

title: VERIFY: Firecracker host-listener semantics for multiple ports
description:
PARTIALLY answered by m80-tv7i.1 verification (2026-05-04). Remaining
work narrowed to confirming concurrent multi-port operation works for
ONE VM.

## Already verified (see docs/verifications/m80-tv7i.1-vsock-companion-file.md)

1. Source: `firecracker/src/vmm/src/devices/virtio/vsock/unix/muxer.rs:619-641`
   — `handle_peer_request_pkt` does
   `UnixStream::connect(format!("{}_{}", host_sock_path, dst_port))`
   on every guest-initiated outbound. The host must already be listening
   at that path.
2. Source: `muxer.rs:99-104` doc-comment confirms `<path>_<port>` is the
   convention for "Unix sockets listening on specific ports".
3. The same `host_sock_path` is reused for any port the guest connects
   out to — no per-port REST setup. The mechanism supports any number
   of host listener paths under one vsock device.

## Remaining open question

Does Firecracker correctly route concurrent guest-outbound connections
to multiple host listeners under one vsock device? In principle yes
(line 620 just constructs a different `port_path` per packet), but
worth a fixture: bind two host listeners (`vsock.sock_9000` and
`vsock.sock_9001`), have a test guest do outbound to both at startup,
verify both `accept()`s return.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Fixture under `m80-firecracker/tests/` with two host listeners,
      one for ready-port, one for a synthetic second port.
- [ ] Test guest (could be a small modification to m80-guestd test
      harness) does `vsock::VsockStream::connect(VMADDR_CID_HOST=2, P)`
      for each port at startup.
- [ ] Both accepts return; both reads succeed.
- [ ] No code lands from this leaf — observation only. Result feeds
      into m80-7tpy.2 (DESIGN) before IMPL.
close_reason: subsumed by tv7i.1 source-code verification + production validation

title: DESIGN: Settle wire — READY_PORT, host-listener path, version byte
description:
Pin the implementation contract before IMPL leaves start. Most
decisions already made by parent description rewrite (2026-05-04).

## Decisions to lock

1. **READY_PORT constant**. Suggestion: `9000` (one below exec port
   9001). Defined in `m80-proto::version` as `READY_PORT_DEFAULT: u32`.
2. **Where the host binds the listener**. Suggestion:
   `m80-jailer::Plan::compute` adds a CreateInsideJail step for the
   listener's parent path; m80-firecracker's
   `phase_4_jailer_materialize` binds the `UnixListener` at
   `<jail>/vsock.sock_<READY_PORT>` and stores the FD on
   `MaterializedJail` for `phase_12b` to consume.
3. **Wire payload from guest**. Single byte:
   `m80_proto::PROTOCOL_VERSION as u8`. Mismatch surfaces as a new
   `VsockError::ProtocolVersionMismatch { expected: u8, got: u8 }`.
4. **Deadline**. Reuse `READY_TIMEOUT` from `launch.rs`. Listener's
   `accept()` is non-blocking; phase_12b polls `accept()` with a
   short epoll timeout per iteration.
5. **Fallback**. None. If `accept()` times out, surface
   `VsockError::NotReady` like today. The CONNECT/OK probe is no
   longer needed for readiness; remove `Channel::open_uds_only`'s
   role in phase_12b but keep the helper for the actual exec
   handshake later.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Three constants merged in m80-proto: `READY_PORT_DEFAULT`,
      `READY_PORT_PROTOCOL_VERSION_BYTE` (alias for `PROTOCOL_VERSION
      as u8`), `READY_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` (probably 5s, separate from
      `READY_TIMEOUT` which is the overall phase_12b budget).
- [ ] `VsockError::ProtocolVersionMismatch` variant added.
- [ ] m80-vsock README documents the new ready-listener contract.
- [ ] No phase_12b changes yet (that's IMPL host leaf .4).
close_reason: design locked in parent description; implemented in ad00c02

title: IMPL guestd: outbound connect to host CID 2 + write proto-version byte at startup
description:
Depends on m80-7tpy.2 (DESIGN). Implement the guestd side of the
inverted-readiness handshake.

## Change site

`crates/m80-guestd/src/main.rs` — between the inbound `bind` on
GUEST_PORT_DEFAULT (line ~57) and the existing
`println!(READY_MARKER_DEFAULT)` ready-marker (line ~61).

## Behavior

1. After `VsockListener::bind_with_cid_port(VMADDR_CID_ANY, port)`
   succeeds, open `VsockStream::connect_with_cid_port(VMADDR_CID_HOST,
   READY_PORT)`.
2. Write exactly one byte: `m80_proto::PROTOCOL_VERSION as u8`.
3. Flush; close (drop the stream). No reads — host already knows
   we're ready by the time the byte lands.
4. If the connect fails or the write fails, **exit non-zero** with a
   typed error logged. We don't want guestd to silently start
   listening when the host can't see it; the host's own deadline
   will surface the problem, but a fast guest-side abort produces
   better diagnostics.

## What stays the same

- Keep the `println!(READY_MARKER_DEFAULT)` print to the serial
  console for now. Removing it is a separate cleanup once the host
  side is migrated and we've verified no third path watches the
  marker.
- The vsock crate dependency is already present
  (`vsock::VsockListener` is imported; add `VsockStream`).

## Tests

- Unit test in `crates/m80-guestd/tests/` (or co-located if simpler)
  that drives a fake host UDS via `socat` or
  `nix::sys::socket` and verifies one byte == PROTOCOL_VERSION
  arrives.
- Negative test: with no host listener, the connect fails and the
  process returns non-zero (test as a child process via
  `assert_cmd` if guestd already uses it; otherwise document
  that this is covered end-to-end in the smoke test).

## Out of scope

- Removing the console-marker println — see CHANGELOG entry in
  m80-7tpy.6.
- Host-side accept; that's m80-7tpy.4.
notes: Implemented in commit ad00c02. m80-guestd outbound connect to (VMADDR_CID_HOST, READY_PORT_DEFAULT=52525) with PROTOCOL_VERSION byte, after vsock listener bind, before main accept loop. Failure is fatal.
close_reason: implemented (ad00c02)

title: IMPL host: replace phase_12b polling with accept() + version-byte read
description:
Depends on m80-7tpy.2 (DESIGN) and m80-7tpy.3 (guestd impl). Replace
the polling loop in `phase_12b_ready_probe` with a deadline-bound
accept on the ready socket.

## Change site

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:411-447` — `phase_12b_ready_probe`.

## Behavior

1. Before `InstanceStart` (i.e., earlier in launch.rs than today's
   phase_12b), bind a `UnixListener` on
   `<jail_path>/vsock.sock_<READY_PORT>`. Set non-blocking or
   accept-timeout so the deadline is enforceable.
   - If m80-7tpy.1 found we need a separate REST PUT for the
     listener port, do that instead/also here.
2. After `InstanceStart`, `accept()` with a deadline (READY_TIMEOUT,
   today's 30s but consider lowering — this is event-driven so the
   wait is bounded by guest boot, not poll-interval-quantized).
3. On `accept()`:
   - Read exactly one byte with a 5s read deadline.
   - Compare against `PROTOCOL_VERSION as u8`.
   - On mismatch, return
     `VsockError::IncompatibleProtoVersion { expected, got }` —
     no exec channel is opened. Tear down.
4. On success: drop the ready socket; proceed to
   `Channel::open_uds_only(vsock_uds, GUEST_PORT_DEFAULT)` exactly
   as today. The exec channel is the same as before.

## Error variants

- New `VsockError` variant for proto-version mismatch (mirror
  ProtoError; one variant — don't add a generic "PreflightFailed").
- Reuse `VsockError::NotReady` for the deadline case.

## Tests

- Unit test with a hand-rolled mock guestd (a thread that connects
  to the UDS and writes one byte) that verifies the host accepts
  and validates within the deadline.
- Test for proto-version mismatch: write `0xff` instead of
  `PROTOCOL_VERSION` and assert the host returns
  `IncompatibleProtoVersion`.
- Test for accept timeout: don't connect at all, assert
  `NotReady` after the deadline.

## Out of scope

- Choosing READY_TIMEOUT. Today's 30s is a reasonable starting
  point; tighten in m80-7tpy.5 once benchmarks land.
- Removing the polling code in phase_12b — this leaf replaces it,
  not gates it behind a feature flag. m80 is v0.1 and we own
  every consumer.
notes: Implemented in commit ad00c02. phase_11b_bind_ready_listener creates UnixListener at <jail>/vsock.sock_52525 before InstanceStart, chowns to jail_uid. phase_12b_ready_accept replaces polled CONNECT/OK probe with accept() + version-byte read.
close_reason: implemented (ad00c02)

title: BENCH: m80-7tpy vs m80-tv7i+m80-6gv9 — pick the winner
description:
Validate event-driven readiness beats the polling backstop (m80-bgas).

## Background

m80-tv7i and m80-6gv9 (the original alternative paths this bench was
meant to compare against) are both closed `--reason "premise-refuted"`
or `"superseded"`. The remaining comparison is m80-7tpy
(event-driven via `accept()`) vs m80-bgas (10ms-poll CONNECT/OK
backstop).

## Bench harness

On a real KVM host:
1. Run `scripts/smoke.sh launch-only` 30 times with the m80-bgas
   constants (10ms poll, 60s timeout). Record P50/P95 of "InstanceStart
   REST PUT → vsock channel ready".
2. Same, with m80-7tpy enabled.
3. Repeat both under host load (`stress-ng --cpu 8` running
   in parallel).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] m80-7tpy idle-host P50 ≤ 50ms above guest kernel boot floor.
- [ ] m80-7tpy P95-vs-P50 spread ≤ 2× (low jitter is the point of
      event-driven).
- [ ] m80-7tpy under stress: P95 within 1.5× of idle P95 (graceful
      degradation; polling would degrade linearly with host load).
- [ ] Numbers added to CHANGELOG and to m80-vsock README.

## Out of scope

- Comparing to smolvm directly. Per recon doc 03, smolvm uses 10ms
  stat-poll on a virtiofs marker — they're not on firecracker, so
  it's apples-to-oranges. The relevant differentiator is m80-7tpy's
  event-driven design, not a head-to-head latency number.

title: m80 env --json: diagnostic dump command (host capabilities + config + versions)
description:
Modeled on kata-ctl env. Single subcommand printing host capability + runtime config + hypervisor version + kernel/image paths in a format-versioned JSON envelope.

## Reference

kata-exploration/10-dx-docs-config.md. kata-ctl env dumps: host info (kernel, CPU, memory, vsock support, KVM capability), runtime config (paths, debug flags), hypervisor info (version via subprocess, machine type), image/kernel paths. Output as TOML or JSON with a format-versioned envelope.

## Why

Bug reports today require asking the user to gather scattered facts (uname, kvm-ok, firecracker --version, m80 config show, ls of run-root). One command should produce a complete dump.

## Scope

- m80 env --json: emits {"version": 1, "data": {...}} envelope.
- Captures: kernel version, /dev/kvm accessibility, vsock kernel module, CPU count + flags relevant to KVM, total memory, current m80 config (effective after layering), firecracker version (subprocess if discoverable), kernel + rootfs paths from manifest, m80-cli version, run-root state if present.
- m80 env (no flag): human-readable equivalent.
- Format-versioned: every consumer reads `data.version` first.

## Out of scope

- Auto-uploading dumps anywhere.
- Live VM inspection (that's m80 inspect).

## Acceptance

- m80 env --json produces a single JSON document parseable by jq.
- README documents the command and points at it from a "filing a bug" section.
- A bug-report template can curl the output into an issue.

title: Test-time auto-dump: on test failure, surface <run_dir>/console.log + diagnostics.jsonl
description:
Make test failures self-explaining. Today an integration-test failure leaves logs in /tmp/.../run_dir; you have to know to look. A wrapper that dumps relevant artifacts on failure makes flakes (and real bugs) cheap to triage.

## Why

Flake debugging cost is dominated by "where are the logs for that run." A drop-on-fail helper makes that cost zero. Compounds with every other observability bead.

## Scope

- Test helper in m80-firecracker (or a tests/common/ module) that wraps integration-test setup; on test panic / assertion failure, prints last N lines of <run_dir>/console.log and the full <run_dir>/diagnostics.jsonl to test stderr.
- Helper is opt-in (callers wrap the test body in a guard); not a global panic hook to avoid suppressing real bugs.
- Truncate console.log dump to a sane size (e.g. last 100 lines) but always full diagnostics.jsonl (small).
- Include the run_dir path in the dump so the user can re-inspect.

## Out of scope

- Auto-uploading to anywhere.
- Capturing host-side strace / perf data (out-of-band tools).

## Acceptance

- A deliberately-failing integration test produces a readable artifact dump in cargo test output.
- A passing test produces nothing extra.
- One canonical test demonstrates the helper.
notes: Implemented 2026-05-05. RunDirDumpGuard at crates/m80-firecracker/tests/common/mod.rs uses Drop + std::thread::panicking() check; testable dump_run_dir(&Path, usize, &mut dyn Write) factored out so unit tests can capture+assert on output via Vec<u8> sink. 8 unit tests cover all scenarios. Missing files surface as '(not found)' lines, not swallowed.

title: request_id end-to-end: CLI → host events → guest stderr → diagnostics.jsonl
description:
A single opaque request_id assigned at the CLI invocation flows through every layer. Without it, host events and guest stderr cannot be aligned for any non-trivial debug session.

## Reference

CLAUDE.md scope: "m80's wire carries an opaque request_id at most" — this bead delivers that. kata-exploration/07-public-api-and-shim.md notes kata's ttRPC has a metadata KV slot it leaves unpopulated despite running OTel — they paid the abstraction without using it. Don't repeat.

## Scope

- m80-cli generates a request_id (UUIDv7 or ULID for ordering) at command entry; binary edge.
- m80-firecracker accepts a request_id parameter at the orchestration entry points (launch, exec, stop, delete) and threads it into:
  - tracing spans (so logs already have it)
  - diagnostics.jsonl every event (new request_id field)
  - the wire frame to m80-guestd
- m80-guestd includes request_id in every stderr line (the structured boot_log format from the guest-log-surface epic m80-1f8.5).
- ExecResponse / wire responses echo the request_id back so the caller can tie response to invocation.

## Acceptance

- A failed launch can be reconstructed from a single request_id grep across <run_dir>/diagnostics.jsonl + <run_dir>/console.log.
- The CLI prints the request_id on entry (or on error) so users can paste it in a bug report.
- Test: launch a VM, fail it deliberately, grep request_id, confirm appearance in 3 places (host events, guest console, response payload).

## Coordinates with

- m80-1f8.5 (guest-side log surface) — guestd needs the request_id available to stamp lines.
- m80-1f8.1 (diagnostics event log) — schema additive change.
- m80-bpuf (JSON envelope) — request_id should appear in the envelope alongside version.

title: Quick wins in phase_12b_ready_probe — 10ms poll, 60s timeout
description:
Cheap parity backstop independent of m80-7tpy: tighten the existing
CONNECT/OK polling loop in `phase_12b_ready_probe`. Lands risk-free.

## Today

- READY_POLL_INTERVAL: 500 ms
- READY_TIMEOUT: 30 s

## Proposed (revised after smolvm recon)

- READY_POLL_INTERVAL: **10 ms** (was 100 ms in the original bead).
  Smolvm polls at 10 ms (`smolvm/src/process.rs:22` and
  `smolvm/src/agent/manager.rs:1457` per recon doc 03). Each
  `Channel::open_uds_only` attempt costs ~10 ms on success and the
  5 s read timeout caps failed attempts, so even 10 ms intervals leave
  room.
- READY_TIMEOUT: 60 s (matches smolvm's tolerance for slow hosts).

## Why 10 ms is safe

Each `Channel::open_uds_only` attempt does:
1. `UnixStream::connect` to vsock.sock (microseconds when guestd not up;
   succeeds + completes handshake quickly when it is)
2. Read banner / OK with 5 s read timeout

Failed attempts return immediately (ECONNREFUSED on connect, or fall
through to error after the muxer rejects). Successful attempts return
in ~10 ms. So 10 ms polling adds at worst 1 wasted RTT per probe,
which is fine.

## Relationship to m80-7tpy

m80-7tpy supersedes the polling design entirely with `accept()`-based
event-driven readiness. m80-bgas is the BACKSTOP: it lands cheaply
today, gives us most of the win until m80-7tpy lands, and stays as a
fallback path if m80-7tpy ever needs to be disabled.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Constants updated in `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:50-53`.
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry under v0.1.x or v0.2.0.
- [ ] `scripts/smoke.sh` retry loop dropped from 3 attempts to 1.
- [ ] No flake on smoke.sh after the change (verify on idle host).
notes: post-2026-05-04 m80-7tpy: the polled CONNECT/OK probe this bead tuned has been removed entirely. Inverted readiness (event-driven accept) replaced it. The 10ms cadence and 60s timeout are no longer active in code; this bead's optimizations are historical.
close_reason: implemented

title: Tighten READY_POLL_INTERVAL to 10ms and READY_TIMEOUT to 60s

Pure constants change in `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:50-53`.

## Diff (~6 lines)

```rust

```

Plus the doc-comment on `phase_12b_ready_probe` (~lines 420-422)

## Why 10 ms (not 100 ms as originally specified)

Smolvm uses 10 ms (`smolvm/src/process.rs:22`, `smolvm/src/agent/manager.rs:1457`
per recon doc 03). They proved the cadence is safe under real workloads.
We were originally going to match SmolVM-CelestoAI's 100 ms which is
the *Python* SmolVM's TCP-banner cadence — different project. The
target competitor is smol-machines/smolvm at /tank/projects/smolvm,
which uses 10 ms.

title: Format-versioned JSON output envelope for all m80 commands (cross-cutting)
description:
Every m80 command that emits structured output (--json, machine-readable formats) wraps payload in a versioned envelope: {"version": 1, "data": ...}. Free if designed in from the start; expensive to retrofit later.

## Reference

kata-exploration/10-dx-docs-config.md. kata-ctl env emits a format-versioned envelope; consumers can branch on version for schema migrations.

## Why

Consumers (scripts, monitoring agents, m80-adapter) need to detect schema changes. Without a version field, schema migration breaks silently. With one, consumers refuse-or-adapt explicitly.

## Scope

- Define a shared envelope type (probably in m80-cli, possibly in a foundation crate if multiple binaries emit JSON).
- All m80 --json output uses the envelope.
- Document the contract: integer version, monotonically increasing, breaking changes bump it.
- Audit existing --json output points (m80 list, m80 inspect, m80 config show) and migrate.

## Out of scope

- Human-readable output formatting.
- Backwards-compat shims for un-envelope'd output (this lands before any external consumer exists).

## Acceptance

- Every existing --json command emits an enveloped document.
- The new m80 env --json bead (m80-81rw) starts on this from day one.
- README documents the envelope contract.

## Coordinates with

- m80-81rw (env --json) — the first beneficiary.
- m80-6jni epic (DX v0.2) — the README mention belongs there.

title: Stripped guest kernel: minimal config + cmdline trim + init-baked
description:
The firecracker-ci stock kernel takes ~890ms to reach userspace on minimal/idle (P50, m80-f2zc.7 baseline). A purpose-built kernel with the smallest config set m80 needs (vsock, virtio-blk, virtio-net, ext4, overlayfs, devtmpfs; everything else off) plus a trimmed cmdline reaches userspace in ~150-300ms typically — saving 500-700ms per cold launch.

Independent of and complementary to: storage pivot (m80-f2zc) which removes ~700ms of rootfs clone, and snapshot/restore (m80-rrp.3) which skips kernel boot entirely for warm-pool launches but still needs a fast cold boot to fill the pool.

PLAN: docs/planning/agent-roadmap.md (full sequencing).

Sub-leaves:
- DESIGN: lock the kernel config delta (CONFIGs to keep, drop, modify), build environment (Docker? chroot? upstream kernel-build container?), kernel version
- IMPL m80-image-build: kernel build pipeline producing kernels/vmlinux-m80-<sha>.bin; manifest gains a kernel.kind discriminator parallel to image_kind
- IMPL m80-firecracker: cmdline trim — quiet loglevel=0 8250.nr_uarts=0, dropped pci=off duplicate, kept reboot=k panic=-1
- BENCH: measure boot-to-guestd-bind delta on minimal/idle and minimal/loaded; target <300ms
- DOCS: manifest schema bump if needed; README delta in m80-image-build

NON-GOALS: kernel security hardening beyond what minimal CONFIG provides; multi-arch (x86_64 only in v0.2); kernel-source vendoring (use upstream linux.tar.xz).

title: DESIGN: kernel config delta + build environment + version
description:
Pin the contract:

1. Kernel version: latest LTS (5.15.x or 6.1.x) or align with firecracker-ci's track. Decide.
2. CONFIG keep list: CONFIG_VSOCKETS, CONFIG_VIRTIO_VSOCKETS, CONFIG_VIRTIO_BLK, CONFIG_VIRTIO_NET, CONFIG_VIRTIO_MMIO, CONFIG_EXT4_FS, CONFIG_OVERLAY_FS (per m80-f2zc.5), CONFIG_DEVTMPFS, CONFIG_DEVTMPFS_MOUNT, CONFIG_SERIAL_8250, CONFIG_SERIAL_8250_CONSOLE.
3. CONFIG drop list: PCI (CONFIG_PCI=n — we use virtio-mmio), most filesystems (CONFIG_BTRFS, XFS, F2FS, etc.), most network protocols (keep IPv4 only), USB, sound, drm, framebuffer, input, security modules beyond minimum, debugfs, tracing, ftrace, perf, kdb, kgdb, crash kernel.
4. Build environment: a Docker container based on Ubuntu 22.04 with kernel-build tooling (build-essential, bc, flex, bison, libelf-dev, libssl-dev). Reproducible Dockerfile committed to crates/m80-image-build/kernel-builder/.
5. Output convention: crates/m80-image-build/kernels/vmlinux-m80-<config-sha>.bin; manifest schema gains kernel.kind variant.

ACCEPTANCE: doc at docs/design/stripped-kernel.md with config delta, build container, version pin, and target boot time. No code in this leaf.

DEPS: none.
EFFORT: M (1 day; mostly research + decision-locking).

title: M80_DEBUG_WIRE env: dump vsock + firecracker REST traffic at framing layer (dev-only)
description:
Wire-level visibility, on demand, without a rebuild. Today protocol bugs require code edits to add eprintlns at the framing layer. A gated env-var dump would save hours per incident.

## Reference

CLAUDE.md "diagnostics before hypotheses" applies inside the workspace too. Most recent vsock-muxer / readiness investigations would have been minutes shorter with raw frame dumps available on demand.

## Scope

- m80-firecracker-client: when fcrest set, log every REST request method+path+body+response status+body.
- Always gated; never on in release default; documented as "dev/debug only, do not enable in production".
- Output goes to tracing (RUST_LOG=trace picks it up).

- Persistent capture/replay (use existing logs).
- Filtering by request_id at this layer (request_id end-to-end bead handles it elsewhere).

- M80_DEBUG_WIRE=all RUST_LOG=trace m80 launch produces visible frame-level lines.
- Default invocation produces zero such lines.
- README of m80-vsock and m80-firecracker-client document the flag.
