title: Networking — OutboundNat
description:
Purpose: deterministic per-host bridge/tap/IP/MAC allocation, default-deny iptables policy with admitted DNS resolvers and bounded private exceptions, ownership-aware idempotent cleanup.
Contract: bridge/tap names + CIDR + IPv4 + MAC are deterministic functions of (run_root, vm_id) via sha256; collisions fail closed; rules tagged for ownership cleanup; bridge orphans only removed when no peer references them.
Surface: network.rs (3669 LOC, dossier risk #1). Spec'd in v0.1; implementation deferred to v0.2.
Evidence: m80/docs/behaviors/network-outbound-nat/ + m80/<crate>/tests/network-outbound-nat/.

title: Address allocation
description:
Contract: bridge name brfc + first 12 hex of sha256(run_root); bridge CIDR 172.<o2>.<o3>.0/24 from sha256 bytes (o2 = (sha256[0]%16)+16, o3 = sha256[1]); cap of ~4096 non-colliding bridges per host (172.16.0.0/12); tap name tfc + first 12 hex of sha256(run_root+vm_id); guest IPv4 deterministic per (run_root,vm_id); guest MAC 02:+hex of vm_digest[0..5] locally-administered.
Surface: network.rs:Phase 1 functions.
Evidence: m80/docs/behaviors/network-outbound-nat/allocation.md + m80/<crate>/tests/network-outbound-nat/allocation.rs.

title: Derive bridge name from sha256 of run_root path
description:
Behavior: The system computes `bridge_name = "brfc" + first 12 hex chars of sha256(run_root_path)`, yielding a Linux interface name within the 15-byte limit and stable across restarts of the same run-root.
Source: dossier `06-network-internals.md` § Phase 1: planning; predecessor `crates/sandbox/agent-sandbox-firecracker/src/network.rs` `plan_outbound_nat_vm_network` lines 224-289 (specifically line 245).

title: Derive bridge CIDR from sha256 bytes of run_root
description:
Behavior: The system derives the bridge CIDR as `172.<o2>.<o3>.0/24` where `o2 = (sha256(run_root)[0] % 16) + 16` (range 16..31) and `o3 = sha256(run_root)[1]` (range 0..255), with gateway pinned to `172.<o2>.<o3>.1`.

description:
Contract: reject_guest_ipv4_collision scans <run_root>/*/network-state.json for any other VM with this guest IP; reject_host_route_collision reads /proc/net/route and rejects bridge CIDRs overlapping any existing route; collision is a hard error with no random fallback.

title: Crash mid-VM does not break new VM startups
description:
Behavior: The system tolerates crash-mid-`prepare_vm_network` because deterministic naming plus owner-record validation make subsequent VM startups idempotent: a new VM either re-uses the existing bridge (when state matches), scavenges an orphan bridge during `cleanup_orphan_bridge_if_unused`, or surfaces a typed `NetworkAllocationConflict` instead of corrupting peer state.
Source: dossier `06-network-internals.md` § Robustness ("Crash recovery: next VM startup scavenges orphan bridges"); predecessor `crates/sandbox/agent-sandbox-firecracker/src/network.rs` `ensure_bridge_ready` lines 298-303 (existing-bridge path), `validate_expected_bridge_state` lines 709-724, and `cleanup_orphan_bridge_if_unused` lines 1123-1147.
Captured by: m80/docs/behaviors/network-outbound-nat/ownership.md#crash-mid-vm + m80/crates/network/tests/network-outbound-nat/ownership.rs::crash_mid_vm_does_not_break_new_startup

title: rtnetlink crate for tap/bridge/link work in m80-net-outbound (replace ip shellouts)
description:
Replace planned Command::new("ip", ...) shellouts with the rtnetlink crate for tap creation, MAC assignment, link up/down, and bridge attach. Iptables stays shellout (or wrapper crate); kata avoids netlink for it on the host too.

## Reference

kata-exploration/04-networking-architecture.md. Kata's runtime-rs uses the rtnetlink crate for all netlink work; the Go runtime uses vishvananda/netlink. No shellouts to ip / tc except a single ifb0 case in optional rx-rate-limiting.

## Why

Shellouts are slow (process spawn + parse stderr), error-handling is by string matching, and they require the ip binary on the host. rtnetlink is direct kernel ioctls, errors are typed, no host dependency.

## Scope

- Add rtnetlink workspace dependency.
- m80-net-outbound (and any sibling crate doing tap/bridge work) uses rtnetlink for: tap creation, link MAC set, link up/down, bridge add/del/attach, address assignment.
- iptables: keep current shellout approach.
- Update m80-net-outbound README to document the privilege requirement (CAP_NET_ADMIN) and the rtnetlink dependency.

## Out of scope

- Replacing iptables with nftables / netlink-based firewall.
- ifb / tc-filter (kata's only ip-binary shellout — defer).

## Acceptance

- All tap / bridge / link operations in m80-net-outbound go through rtnetlink.
- A regression test exercises tap creation + teardown without invoking /sbin/ip.
- README documents the dependency.

title: Storage pivot: shared RO base + per-VM overlay rootfs
description:
Replace the per-VM full file-copy of the base ext4 (Rootfs::clone, ~727 ms on 256 MiB image) with a shared read-only host-side base file plus a per-VM sparse ext4 overlay assembled in-guest as overlayfs. The host file is presented to every VM as drive 1 with is_read_only: true; the per-VM sparse ext4 is drive 2; an optional workspace ext4 becomes drive 3. m80-guestd, running as PID 1 on the minimal-init image, mounts /dev/vda read-only as the lowerdir, /dev/vdb rw as the upperdir/workdir host, assembles overlayfs at a staging mount, then pivot_roots into it before mounting the workspace at /workspace.

WHY: ~700 ms cold-launch saved; per-VM disk drops from O(base size) to O(actual writes). Firecracker docs explicitly bless this pattern (docs/snapshotting/snapshot-support.md:77). m80-urc.1 (per-VM cloning) closed premise-refuted.

PRIORITY NOTE (2026-05-04): P2 after agent-use-case re-rank — snapshot/restore (m80-rrp.3) is the headline cold-launch unlock; this is complementary architectural cleanup + ~700 ms incremental win, queued behind P1.

PLAN: docs/planning/storage-pivot-bead-plan.md (full leaf descriptions). Exploration: docs/exploration/{kata-containers,firecracker-shared-rootfs,overlayfs-kernel-semantics,runc-crun-overlayfs-init,firecracker-containerd}.md.

NON-GOALS: Multi-layer EROFS stacking. Host-side device-mapper thin pools. tmpfs upper layer. Snapshot-resume integration (complementary, m80-rrp.3). Live writeback. Removing ubuntu/systemd image.

title: DESIGN: lock storage API, drive layout, in-guest mount sequence
description:
Produce a written design that pins, in one place, the contract every other leaf in this epic consumes:

1. m80-storage public surface (final form): Rootfs::prepare(base, overlay_dest, overlay_size_bytes), Rootfs::new_at, Rootfs::base_path, Rootfs::overlay_path. Rootfs::clone and Rootfs::path deleted. Caller verifies base sha256; prepare allocates sparse + mkfs.ext4 -F.

2. Drive layout, PUT order: vda=base RO, vdb=overlay RW, vdc=workspace RW (when present). PUT order matches; is_read_only:true on vda; root is vda; ACPI DSDT order is the documented contract (firecracker-shared-rootfs.md §2).

3. In-guest sequence (PID 1): the 11-step mount/pivot pseudocode from overlayfs-kernel-semantics.md is normative — MS_REC|MS_PRIVATE on /, mount vda RO at /lower, vdb at /upper, mkdir /upper/root and /upper/.work, mount overlay at /merged, mount /proc /sys /dev INTO /merged, MS_SLAVE|MS_REC on /, bind /merged onto itself, pivot_root('.','.') per kata, MNT_DETACH old root, then mount /dev/vdc at /workspace inside the new root.

4. Failure policy: overlay mount or pivot failure as PID 1 panics (no kernel panic recovery; run-dir preserved). No retry.

5. Sparse overlay sizing: default 512 MiB sparse; configurable via SandboxConfig::overlay_size_bytes.

ACCEPTANCE: doc landed at docs/design/storage-overlay.md with API signatures, drive table, pseudocode in code blocks. Cross-references to four exploration docs. Both crates/m80-storage/README.md and crates/m80-firecracker/README.md (already drafted) reconciled. No code in this leaf — contract leaf.

EFFORT: S (3-4 hours). Captures decisions made in exploration docs.
close_reason: implemented

title: IMPL m80-storage: prepare(base, overlay_dest, size); delete clone()
description:
Replace Rootfs::clone(base, dest) with Rootfs::prepare(base, overlay_dest, overlay_size_bytes). prepare allocates a sparse file at overlay_dest (File::create + set_len — sparse on ext4/xfs/tmpfs by default), then shells out mkfs.ext4 -F. Returns Rootfs { base, overlay }. Add base_path() and overlay_path() accessors. Delete Rootfs::clone, Rootfs::path(), BaseSha256Mismatch and CopyRootfs error variants, and any sha256-on-clone behavior — per the README, base verification is the caller's job (m80_image_manifest::Manifest::verify), not Rootfs's.

ACCEPTANCE:
- crates/m80-storage/src/lib.rs: Rootfs::prepare, new_at, base_path, overlay_path present; clone and path absent. mkfs.ext4 -F shellout via existing Command pattern; bubble exit code as StorageError::Mkfs.
- crates/m80-storage/tests/rootfs_prepare.rs: at least four #[test] fns — sparse-overlay creation succeeds, base path preserved, overlay is valid ext4 (file <overlay> or read superblock magic), new_at() returns paths without I/O, missing-base path produces StorageError::Io.
- README 'Public surface (full)' matches code 1:1. Run cargo test -p m80-storage clean.

EFFORT: M (1 day). Small surface but every consumer must rebuild.

title: IMPL m80-firecracker: three-drive PUT in PUT-order with is_read_only on base
description:
Update boot-phase block-device PUT sequence to:
1. PUT rootfs with is_read_only:true and is_root_device:true, host_path = Rootfs::base_path()
2. PUT rootfs_overlay with is_read_only:false, host_path = Rootfs::overlay_path()
3. PUT workspace with is_read_only:false, host_path = Scratch::path(), only when SandboxConfig::workspace_dir.is_some()

Order is load-bearing: Firecracker assigns vda/vdb/vdc by PUT order (firecracker-shared-rootfs.md §2). Base file is bind-mounted into the jailer chroot exactly as today; nothing changes about the jailer surface beyond an extra bind-mount for the overlay file.

ACCEPTANCE:
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs phase_11_rest_puts: three drive PUTs in specified order; is_read_only field set explicitly per drive (no defaulting).
- Integration test (root-required, gated #[ignore]): launch a VM, attach to admin socket, GET drives, assert vda is RO and vdb/vdc are RW.
- README drive-layout table reconciled if needed (already drafted).

DEPS: m80-storage IMPL must land first (provides Rootfs::base_path/overlay_path).

EFFORT: S (4 hours). Mechanical PUT-order refactor.
notes: commit=30cff7c; phase_11 PUT vda+vdb+vdc per overlay design; Rootfs::clone replaced with Rootfs::prepare; SandboxConfig::overlay_size_bytes added (default 512 MiB); RunningSandbox::run_dir() accessor added; README updated

title: Generic Wire Protocol
description:
Purpose: opaque request/response wire over vsock with NDJSON framing and version handshake. Generic — no tool_call_id, correlation_id, or idempotency_key semantics (agent concerns); at most an opaque request_id round-trip.
Contract: NDJSON one-doc-per-line with 4 MiB ceiling; version byte explicit; mismatch fails closed.
Surface: agent-guest-proto/envelope.rs (reframed).
Evidence: m80/docs/behaviors/wire-protocol/ + m80/<crate>/tests/wire-protocol/.

title: Audit: typed error variants visible at m80-cli + m80-firecracker public surface (no string collapse)
description:
Sweep public error surfaces and ensure typed thiserror variants stay typed at the boundary. Don't collapse to string-wrapped Other / Generic on the way out (kata's mistake at the ttRPC shim boundary).

## Reference

kata-exploration/07-public-api-and-shim.md. Kata's internal errors are typed (ContainerNotFound, ProcessNotFound, AgentConnectionClosed), but at the shim boundary they collapse to ttrpc::Error::Others(string) — losing type information for consumers. m80 should not repeat this.

## Why

CLAUDE.md ("What we don't want") forbids reclassification that hides which call site lost the file; the same principle applies to error type collapse. m80-cli's class-based exit codes (EXIT_PREFLIGHT=2 etc.) only work if the underlying error variants are still discriminable.

## Scope

- Audit m80-firecracker public Error type: are all variants concrete? any "Other(String)" / "Generic"?
- Audit m80-cli error mapping (m80-cli/src/errors.rs): does every internal error variant map cleanly to an exit code, or do some funnel through a string wrapper?
- Where collapse exists, replace with concrete variants.
- Document the policy in CLAUDE.md ("What we don't want") if not already covered.

## Out of scope

- Internal-only error types (those can be richer; the audit is at the public boundary only).
- anyhow at binary edges is fine (that's already the policy).

## Acceptance

- m80-firecracker::Error has no String-wrapping fallback variant (or has one with a written justification).
- m80-cli error → exit-code mapping is exhaustive over the underlying error type (compile-time match coverage).
- One regression test pins at least one specific error → specific exit code.

title: Audit: #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] across all m80 config / manifest types
description:
Sweep m80 for serde-deserialized types where unknown fields should fail loudly instead of silently dropping. Bug found during kata recon: BuildConfig in crates/m80-image-build/src/config.rs is missing #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)].

## Reference

kata-exploration/05-image-build-and-rootfs.md flagged m80-image-build/src/config.rs as a concrete miss.

## Why

With the missing attribute, a typo in a config field name silently drops the value. CLAUDE.md ("What we don't want") explicitly forbids "be tolerant" wrappers on internal data. A typo should be a parse error, not silent acceptance.

## Scope

- Grep all #[derive(Deserialize)] in the workspace.
- Add #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] to every internal config / manifest / wire type unless there is a specific written reason not to (e.g. the m80-image-manifest schema if it has a forward-compat clause — but verify).
- Add a regression test for at least m80-image-build BuildConfig: unknown field → error.
- Document the policy in CLAUDE.md's "What we don't want" section if absent.

## Out of scope

- External-facing wire formats with explicit forward-compat semantics. Verify each before applying.

## Acceptance

- All internal config / manifest types either have the attribute or have a one-line comment explaining why not.
- One regression test pinning the BuildConfig case.

title: m80 logs <vm>: unified tail of guest console + host diagnostics
description:
Single subcommand that tails (or dumps) the guest console.log + host diagnostics.jsonl interleaved, filtered by request_id.

## Reference

CLAUDE.md "diagnostics before hypotheses": the first move on any failure should be "see what the guest said." Today there is no command for that.

## Scope

- m80 logs <vm-id> [--follow] [--request-id <id>] [--since <ts>].
- Reads <run_dir>/console.log and <run_dir>/diagnostics.jsonl.
- Interleaves by timestamp; tags each line with [host] or [guest].
- Filter by request_id if provided.
- --json mode emits structured records using the m80-bpuf envelope.

## Out of scope

- Live streaming from inside a running VM (vsock log-channel) — that's the job of the guest-log-surface bead's console capture.
- Querying logs across multiple VMs (defer; m80 inspect --all does enumeration).

## Acceptance

- m80 logs <vm> on a stopped VM dumps the full interleaved log.
- m80 logs --follow on a running VM streams new lines as they appear.
- --json output validates against the envelope schema.
- Filter by request_id returns only matching lines (zero false positives).

## Coordinates with

- m80-1f8.5 (guest-side log surface) — produces console.log.
- request_id end-to-end bead — provides the filter dimension.
- m80-bpuf (envelope) — defines --json shape.

title: Adapter ecosystem & agent surface
description: Purpose: ship the agent-facing layer ON TOP of m80's generic core, so m80 stays auditable while the agent UX matches or beats SmolVM. Scope decision (2026-05-03): the originally-planned external 'm80-adapter' moves in-tree as 'm80-adapter'. Agent semantics (tool catalog, idempotency, semantic events) remain OUT of m80 itself per CLAUDE.md scope; they live in this adapter layer. Strategic context: SmolVM (CelestoAI, shipped Apr 2026) owns 'Python AI sandbox'. m80's edge is Rust-embeddable + audit-small + generic foundation. Adapter ecosystem extends reach without contaminating the core: m80-adapter (Rust agent surface), m80-py (PyO3 Python bindings), CLI agent mode.

title: Snapshot-restore launch path: 0-boot via firecracker snapshot
description:
Wire m80-snapshot's capture()/restore() execution lane to Firecracker's snapshot REST endpoints. Today the schemas + persistence-path helpers are active in v0.1 but capture() and restore() return SnapshotError::Deferred; this bead replaces those stubs with real plumbing.

## Scope

Snapshot CAPTURE/RESTORE PLUMBING ONLY. Specifically:

- m80-firecracker-client: add put_snapshot_create + put_snapshot_load REST methods + their config types (CreateSnapshot, LoadSnapshot)
- m80-snapshot: real capture() that pauses the VM, calls CreateSnapshot, writes the manifest + restore-metadata, and verifies the artifact set; real restore() that reads the manifest, validates compat (firecracker version + image identity), and orchestrates the LoadSnapshot REST call
- m80-firecracker: a Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot(...) alternative path that skips the cold-boot phases (3,4 partial,11) and instead PUTs LoadSnapshot then InstanceStart-from-snapshot, joining the regular Phase 12b ready-probe path
- m80-cli: m80 launch --from-snapshot <path> wired to the new code path
- Bench: P50/P95 of restore-launched ready latency on idle + loaded host
- Docs: suitability bounds (stale clocks, pre-baked process trees) + compat-check decisions

## NOT in scope (other m80-rrp children)

- Warm-pool management (allocator that holds N pre-restored VMs ready)
- Eviction policy / pool sizing / refill triggers
- Allocation contract surface (lease / handoff to caller)
- Reset-evidence vocabulary integration with restored VMs

This bead delivers the primitive; m80-rrp.4+ (TBD) consumes it for warm pools.

## Acceptance

- m80-firecracker-client exposes put_snapshot_create + put_snapshot_load with fixture-server tests
- m80-snapshot capture() and restore() return Ok in happy-path; SnapshotError::Deferred is removed
- A Sandbox can be launched from a captured snapshot end-to-end on real-KVM (gated behind the existing end_to_end_real_kvm flag)
- m80 launch --from-snapshot <path> works in the CLI
- Bench numbers landed in docs/behaviors/snapshot/restore-latency.md
- README updates for m80-snapshot (capture/restore active), m80-firecracker-client (snapshot endpoints), m80-firecracker (launch_from_snapshot), m80-cli

## Open design questions, captured in leaves

- Capture preconditions: does the VM need to be Paused? Is snapshot a stop-the-world primitive vs concurrent? (DESIGN leaf)
- Compat checks at restore: firecracker version (already in RestoreMetadata), kernel sha, rootfs sha, machine-config (vcpu/mem) — what's the minimum viable check, what produces silent corruption on mismatch? (DESIGN leaf)
- Vsock state across snapshot: does the in-VM guestd's vsock channel survive a snapshot/restore? (research leaf, may overlap with DESIGN)
- Are CreateSnapshot/LoadSnapshot covered by Firecracker's stable API guarantees, or version-pinned? (DESIGN leaf)

## Relationship

This + minimal-init (m80-6a0q) together get end-to-end agent-ready VMs in roughly 300ms steady-state. SmolVM has snapshots too at ~500ms; with both pieces m80 should beat them at roughly half the latency. Warm-pool management on top (other m80-rrp children) makes that latency the steady-state for every exec, not just the second one.
notes: Update 2026-05-04 (post-kata recon): differentiation is stronger than the smolvm framing alone implied. Kata-containers ALSO did not wire firecracker's snapshot REST API — their FC backend's PauseVM/SaveVM/ResumeVM are silent no-ops; their 'VM factory' is QEMU-only and uses QEMU migration machinery (migrate exec:cat>file), not snapshot. No production runtime we surveyed (smolvm libkrun, kata-containers) has a working firecracker snapshot lifecycle. m80-rrp.3 is unclaimed territory in the firecracker microVM space. See kata-exploration/09-snapshot-templates-lifecycle.md and kata-exploration/00-synthesis.md.

title: DESIGN: snapshot capture/restore preconditions and compat-check matrix
description:
Pin down the Firecracker REST contract for CreateSnapshot/LoadSnapshot before writing client or orchestrator code. Output is a doc at docs/behaviors/snapshot/firecracker-rest-contract.md plus design notes on each open question.

## Topics to nail down

1. CAPTURE preconditions
   - Does the VM need to be in Paused state before CreateSnapshot? (Firecracker docs say yes — confirm and note exact REST sequence.)
   - Is snapshot a stop-the-world primitive (vCPU paused, memory frozen) or can it run concurrently? Document the stall window callers see.
   - What CreateSnapshot fields exist (snapshot_path, mem_file_path, snapshot_type [Full/Diff], version)? Map them to SnapshotManifest artifact paths.

2. RESTORE preconditions
   - LoadSnapshot REST flow: which PUTs are skipped vs still required (boot-source, drives, vsock — does any of this come from the snapshot, or must we re-PUT)?
   - LoadSnapshot fields (snapshot_path, mem_backend [File/Uffd], enable_diff_snapshots, resume_vm).
   - What state is the VM in immediately after LoadSnapshot — Paused, Running, or do we need a separate Resume action?
   - vsock state across snapshot: does the in-VM guestd's vsock channel survive? If not, we need a guestd reconnection protocol — out of scope here, capture as a follow-up bead.

3. COMPAT MATRIX at restore time
   - expected_firecracker_version is already in RestoreMetadata. Must restore() reject mismatches? (Yes — Firecracker doesn't guarantee snapshot compat across versions.)
   - kernel sha: if the captured-VM's kernel differs from the to-restore kernel, what fails (silent corruption vs guaranteed crash)? Add kernel_sha256 to RestoreMetadata?
   - rootfs sha: same question — restore on a different rootfs is almost certainly broken.
   - machine-config: vcpu_count + mem_size_mib must match the captured VM. Add to RestoreMetadata?
   - Recommendation for v0.2: minimum compat check is firecracker_version + kernel_sha + mem_size_mib. Document the gaps and what they protect against.

4. ARTIFACT path layout
   - Map ArtifactKind variants (BootIdentity, Memory, RuntimeRootfs, VmState, WorkspaceScratch) to concrete on-disk filenames inside the persistence dir. SnapshotManifest already names them; pin the file basenames here so capture() and restore() agree.

## Output

- docs/behaviors/snapshot/firecracker-rest-contract.md — the REST flow
- Updates to RestoreMetadata schema if compat fields need adding (do this here, before the impl leaves; schema changes are cheap pre-impl)
- A research note on vsock-across-snapshot (likely 'guestd must reconnect; out of scope for this bead — file follow-up')

## Tests

- Schema-roundtrip update if RestoreMetadata gains fields
- No code-runtime tests in this leaf — it's a design output that the IMPL leaves consume.

## Dependencies

Blocks all IMPL leaves under m80-rrp.3.

title: IMPL m80-snapshot: replace Deferred in capture() and restore() with real wiring
description:
Replace the SnapshotError::Deferred stubs in m80-snapshot::capture() and m80-snapshot::restore() with real implementations that call through m80-firecracker-client.

## capture() new signature (proposed; refine in DESIGN leaf)

pub fn capture(running: &mut RunningSandbox, store_root: &Path) -> Result<SnapshotManifest, SnapshotError>

## capture() semantics

1. Pause the VM (InstanceAction::Pause via running's existing Client).
2. Compute the persistence path (use existing persistence_path helper).
3. Resolve destination collision -> SnapshotError::DestinationCollision (do NOT silently overwrite).
4. PUT /snapshot/create with snapshot_path = <dest>/vmstate, mem_file_path = <dest>/memory.
5. Capture/copy the runtime rootfs clone + workspace scratch into the dest dir (these are live ext4 files; consider O_RDONLY copy or fs-level snapshot — DESIGN leaf decides).
6. Compute artifact set sha256s, build SnapshotManifest, write manifest + RestoreMetadata.
7. Resume the VM (InstanceAction::Resume).
8. Return the manifest.

## restore() new signature

pub fn restore(snapshot_dir: &Path, expected_firecracker_version: &str, expected_kernel_sha: Option<&str>) -> Result<RestoreMetadata, SnapshotError>

restore() in m80-snapshot is the manifest-validation + compat-check half. The actual REST orchestration lives in m80-firecracker (next leaf). This split keeps m80-snapshot dependency-free of the orchestrator.

## restore() semantics

1. Read snapshot-manifest.json + restore-metadata.json (existing helpers).
2. Verify all artifact sha256s against on-disk files (NEW — schema is active in v0.1 but verify-on-read is a v0.2 contract per the README).
3. Compat check: expected_firecracker_version + (optional) expected_kernel_sha against RestoreMetadata. Fail-closed with new SnapshotError variants:
   - FirecrackerVersionMismatch { expected, found }
   - KernelShaMismatch { expected, found }
   - Sha256Mismatch { artifact: ArtifactKind, expected, found }
4. Return RestoreMetadata for the orchestrator to consume.

## SnapshotError additions

- FirecrackerVersionMismatch { expected: String, found: String }
- KernelShaMismatch { expected: String, found: String }
- Sha256Mismatch { artifact: ArtifactKind, expected: String, found: String }
- (consider) PauseFailed / ResumeFailed for the capture side; alternatively reclassify firecracker-client errors via #[from]. CLAUDE.md prefers symmetric reclassification — pick one and apply uniformly.

The README explicitly notes Sha256Mismatch + FirecrackerVersionMismatch are NOT v0.1 — this leaf is the v0.2 promotion.

## Tests

- tests/capture_happy_path.rs — fixture firecracker UDS server records the Pause/CreateSnapshot/Resume sequence; asserts artifact files exist + sha256s match.
- tests/restore_compat_check.rs — manifest with mismatched expected_firecracker_version returns FirecrackerVersionMismatch; same for kernel sha.
- tests/restore_artifact_sha_mismatch.rs — tamper with one artifact byte; restore returns Sha256Mismatch carrying the offending ArtifactKind.
- Drop tests/deferred_capture_and_restore.rs (Deferred is going away).

## Dependencies

- DESIGN leaf m80-rrp.3.1 (preconditions + compat fields)
- IMPL leaf m80-rrp.3.2 (firecracker-client snapshot methods)
- m80-snapshot now depends on m80-firecracker-client. Update Cargo.toml + README's Dependencies section.

## Acceptance

- capture() and restore() return Ok in happy path
- All three Mismatch error variants exist + are exercised by tests
- README updated: capture/restore section moves from 'deferred' to 'active'; remove the v0.1/v0.2 split language
- cargo test -p m80-snapshot passes

title: IMPL m80-firecracker: Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot alternative path + Sandbox::capture_running
description:
Wire the snapshot capture/restore execution lane through the orchestrator. Two surfaces:

1. RunningSandbox::capture(&mut self, store_root: &Path) -> Result<SnapshotManifest, FcError> — pauses the VM, calls m80-snapshot::capture(), resumes. Thin wrapper; the heavy lifting is in m80-snapshot.

2. Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot(self, snapshot_dir: &Path) -> Result<RunningSandbox, FcError> — alternative to launch() that skips the cold-boot phases.

## launch_from_snapshot phases

Re-uses phases 1 (run-root prep), 2 (lease), 4 (jailer materialize — needs the same kernel + rootfs bind-mounts), 5 (cgroup probe), 8 (api socket path), 9 (jailer exec firecracker), 5b (cgroup create), 10 (open UDS), 12b (ready probe).

REPLACES phase 3 (storage prep) + phase 6/7 (network) + phase 11 (REST PUTs) + phase 12a (InstanceStart):

- Phase 3': storage from snapshot — clone the captured rootfs.ext4 + scratch.ext4 from the snapshot dir into the run-dir (NOT the base rootfs from manifest). Compat check happens in m80-snapshot::restore() before this.
- Phase 11': PUT /snapshot/load (with resume_vm=true, OR resume_vm=false followed by InstanceAction::Resume — DESIGN leaf decides).
- No InstanceStart from snapshot — Firecracker's LoadSnapshot replaces the cold InstanceStart.

## SandboxConfig field

Decision question (resolve in DESIGN leaf): does launch_from_snapshot take snapshot_dir as a separate function arg, or do we add SandboxConfig.from_snapshot: Option<PathBuf> and gate on it inside launch()?

Recommendation: separate function. Cleaner branch-on-config-field pattern is exactly the kind of premature abstraction CLAUDE.md prohibits ('three near-identical lines beat a generic helper'). launch() and launch_from_snapshot() share helpers but are top-level distinct entry points.

## Tests

- tests/launch_from_snapshot_compile.rs — type-system test that the new method exists with the right signature.
- tests/state_machine_compile.rs — extend to cover the snapshot-restore branch.
- tests/end_to_end_real_kvm.rs — extend with a capture-then-restore round-trip test (gated behind the existing real-KVM flag).

## Documentation

- crates/m80-firecracker/README.md — add Sandbox::capture and Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot to public surface; document the phases skipped vs reused.
- src/launch.rs file is ~448 LOC — adding launch_from_snapshot may push it past the 500-line soft limit. If so, split out a launch_from_snapshot.rs sibling module up front rather than waiting for the hard limit.

## Dependencies

- m80-rrp.3.2 (firecracker-client snapshot REST methods)

- RunningSandbox::capture exists and compiles

title: BENCH: P50/P95 of restore-launched ready latency on idle and loaded host
description:
Quantify the steady-state launch-latency win. Establish the numbers that justify the bead. Document them in docs/behaviors/snapshot/restore-latency.md.

## Bench scope

For a fixed (kernel, rootfs, machine-config) golden snapshot:

1. Idle host
   - Cold boot: m80 launch end-to-end (Phase 1 → ready) — P50/P95 over 50 runs.
   - Restore boot: m80 launch --from-snapshot end-to-end — P50/P95 over 50 runs.
   - Report the gap (target: roughly 5-10x; AWS docs say <200ms restore vs 800-1500ms cold).

2. Loaded host
   - Same two measurements while the host is running 8 concurrent VMs at idle.
   - Watch for restore-time tail latency from disk I/O contention (memory file copy is the long pole).

## What to measure precisely

- 'Ready' = phase_12b_ready_probe returns Ok (vsock channel open, guestd handshake completed).
- Bench timing should NOT include CLI parse + preflight; start the timer at Sandbox::launch / Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot call site.
- Capture the per-phase breakdown for 1-2 representative runs (which phase dominates? Probably phase 9 jailer-exec for cold; phase 11' snapshot-load for restore).

## Tooling

- Use criterion or a hand-rolled bench in crates/m80-firecracker/benches/. Real-KVM only — gated behind the same flag as end_to_end_real_kvm.
- Output: P50, P95, P99, mean, stddev. JSON output committed to docs/behaviors/snapshot/restore-latency.json + a markdown summary in restore-latency.md.

## Compare with SmolVM

If feasible, run the same bench script against SmolVM (snapshot mode) on the same host. Report the comparison. If not feasible (SmolVM not installed / different harness), cite SmolVM's published numbers (~500ms snapshot-restore) and frame m80 as 'expected ~2-3x faster steady-state' from the combined m80-rrp.3 + m80-6a0q (minimal-init) work.

## Dependencies

- m80-rrp.3.4 (the launch_from_snapshot path) — required to bench at all
- m80-rrp.3.5 nice-to-have but not required (bench can call the library directly)

## Acceptance

- restore-latency.md committed with idle + loaded P50/P95 numbers
- restore-latency.json committed with raw run data
- Bench harness committed under crates/m80-firecracker/benches/ (or m80-cli/) — re-runnable
- Numbers validate (or refute) the bead's claim of 'steady-state ~300ms'

## Open question

Should this bead also bench warm-pool steady-state? NO — warm-pool is m80-rrp's other children. This bench measures the snapshot-restore primitive in isolation.
notes: expected save: 125-200 ms warm restore vs cold (medium confidence; AWS published <200 ms). Pre-condition: vsock survival research, DESIGN, IMPL leaves landed. Loaded-cell tail latency informs pool sizing (R8 of perf-roadmap-extended.md §3.1).

title: DOCS: suitability bounds, compat matrix, and CHANGELOG entry
description:
The wrapper-up doc work. Make the new surface discoverable and document what restore-launched VMs are and aren't suitable for.

## Output 1: docs/behaviors/snapshot/suitability.md

Document the trade-offs:

- Stale clocks: a snapshot-restored VM resumes with the captured wall-clock — guestd, agents, and any process that cares about 'what time is it' will see a clock that jumped. Useful for short-lived agent execs (seconds to minutes); broken for long-running daemons that sync time, schedule cron, or rely on monotonic clock continuity.
- Pre-baked process tree: every restore reuses the captured VM's pid namespace and process state. Side-effects from the captured boot (named-pipe state, in-memory locks, /tmp content) carry through. Document as 'fine for stateless agents, requires reset-evidence-vocabulary discipline (m80-rrp.1) for reuse-after-mutation'.
- DNS / network state: any cached resolver state from the captured VM is restored. For NoEgress this is a non-issue; for OutboundNat (v0.2) callers should plan to flush.
- Filesystem state: the captured rootfs and scratch are cloned into a fresh per-restore copy, so the guest sees a private writable copy.

## Output 2: docs/behaviors/snapshot/compat-matrix.md

Document the compat checks that restore() enforces and which it doesn't:

- ENFORCED at restore: firecracker_version exact match, kernel_sha256 exact match, mem_size_mib match, vcpu_count match.
- NOT ENFORCED: host kernel version, host CPU microcode, /proc/cpuinfo features (CPUID). Note these as 'undefined behavior on mismatch'.
- (Tighten this list per the DESIGN leaf m80-rrp.3.1 outcome.)

## Output 3: CHANGELOG.md entry

Under the v0.2 section (or wherever appropriate):

- Added: SnapshotCreateConfig + SnapshotLoadConfig + REST methods on m80-firecracker-client (m80-rrp.3.2)
- Added: m80-snapshot::capture and ::restore now active (was Deferred); new error variants FirecrackerVersionMismatch / KernelShaMismatch / Sha256Mismatch (m80-rrp.3.3)
- Added: Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot + RunningSandbox::capture (m80-rrp.3.4)
- Added: m80 launch --from-snapshot and m80 snapshot capture (m80-rrp.3.5)
- Bench: P50 ~300ms restore-launched ready (m80-rrp.3.6) — fill in actual number.

## README updates already-in-other-leaves

Each IMPL leaf already updates its own crate's README (CLAUDE.md mandate). This leaf is for the cross-cutting docs that don't belong to one crate.

## Dependencies

- All other m80-rrp.3 IMPL + BENCH leaves (this is the wrap-up)

## Acceptance

- Both behavior docs committed
- CHANGELOG entry lands with the merge
- A new contributor can read suitability.md and answer 'is snapshot-restore right for my use case' without reading code
notes: EXTEND: explicit known-limitation entries for R4 (stale wall-clock; out of scope for v0.2), R5 (disk footprint per snapshot ≈ vm_mem_mib MiB), R6 (NoEgress only for v0.2; OutboundNat compat is followup). See perf-roadmap-extended.md §3.1.

title: IMPL m80-firecracker: pre-create vsock UDS at snapshot-load time
description:
When you LoadSnapshot, the host vsock UDS that existed at snapshot-capture time is gone (different run-root, different Sandbox instance). The guest's in-memory vsock state still expects the muxer companion files at <host_sock_path>_<port>. The host has to pre-create the listener BEFORE InstanceStart-from-snapshot, otherwise guest-initiated connects fault.

## Scope

- Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot (m80-rrp.3.4) must allocate the vsock UDS path + bind UnixListener for each known port BEFORE issuing the LoadSnapshot REST call.
- The set of "known ports" is whatever the snapshot manifest captured (guestd control port, plus any reserved ports for ready-probe / m80-7tpy).
- Verify that firecracker's muxer accepts a fresh UDS path on snapshot resume; document any constraints in the snapshot manifest schema (m80-snapshot).

## Acceptance

- launch_from_snapshot survives a guest-initiated vsock connect post-restore (host accept() returns).
- A regression test pins this: snapshot a VM with an active vsock connection, restore, verify the guest can reconnect.
- m80-snapshot README documents the host's pre-create responsibility.

## Sibling

Guestd-side companion bead (post-restore connection-drop detection + redial) tracks separately under m80-rrp.3.

title: IMPL m80-guestd: detect post-restore vsock connection drop and redial
description:
After snapshot/restore, any in-flight vsock connection from guestd to host is severed (the host UDS is a fresh inode, even after the host-side pre-create in m80-rrp.3.8). Guestd needs to detect the drop and redial — without panicking, without losing the agent's in-VM state.

## Scope

- Guestd's vsock client: on read/write error indicating peer-closed, attempt redial with bounded backoff.
- Detection mechanism: rely on AF_VSOCK error semantics (likely EPIPE / ECONNRESET); avoid heartbeat-pinging.
- Redial preserves any per-connection state guestd was tracking (request_id correlation, in-flight stream framing).
- Document the edge case: if guestd was streaming exec output when snapshot fired, the partial frame is lost — caller must handle re-exec.

## Acceptance

- A regression test: capture a snapshot mid-execution, restore, verify guestd reconnects and accepts a new request.
- guestd does not exit(1) or panic on vsock peer-close; it retries with bounded backoff and only exits if reconnect fails for >N seconds.
- m80-guestd README documents the post-restore redial contract.

## Sibling

Host-side companion at m80-rrp.3.8.

title: Marker-file readiness probe to beat SmolVM's polling latency
description:
Replace m80-firecracker's `phase_12b_ready_probe` polling loop with a
stat-based marker probe — IF Firecracker actually creates a host-visible
file when m80-guestd binds its vsock listener. Verification is gating;
see leaf 1.

## Background

Today's `phase_12b_ready_probe`
(crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:423):
- Calls `Channel::open_uds_only` (UDS connect + write `CONNECT 9001`
  + read `OK` line) every 500ms with a 30s deadline. The 5s
  read timeout caps each attempt.
- Each successful attempt is roughly a UDS handshake's worth of work.
- Under host load the probe occasionally times out before guestd binds.

SmolVM's `wait_for_ssh`:
- `socket.connect()` + 32-byte banner sniff at 100ms intervals,
  then full handshake once the banner appears. 60s budget.

## Marker-file premise — UNVERIFIED

The dossier hypothesis: when m80-guestd does
`VsockListener::bind((VMADDR_CID_ANY, 9001))`, Firecracker creates the
host-side companion file `<vsock_uds>_<port>` (e.g.
`<jail>/vsock.sock_9001`) inside the chroot, and stat'ing that file is
a near-zero-cost readiness signal.

CAUTION — Firecracker's official vsock docs
(https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/main/docs/vsock.md)
describe `<uds>_<port>` only in the *opposite* direction: as the file
the **host application** is expected to be listening on so that
**guest-initiated** connections can be forwarded by Firecracker. There
is no documented host filesystem artifact created when the guest binds
a port and waits for host-initiated connects (which is the m80
direction). Firecracker's vsock muxer connects to that path; it does
not create one on guest bind.

Leaf 1 (VERIFY) must close this gap before any other leaf is started.
If verification shows the file is not created, the bead pivots:
- Plan A (file-stat probe) is dropped.
- m80-bgas (100ms / 60s constants) ships as the only `phase_12b`
  improvement, and m80-6gv9 (inotify) folds into a new file-watch
  target — likely the serial console + `GUESTD_READY` marker once
  `PUT /logger` is wired (a v0.2 epic).

## Design (conditional on verification passing)

Replace `phase_12b_ready_probe`'s polling loop with two phases:
1. Stat for `<vsock_uds>_<port>` at 10ms intervals (~1µs/probe vs the
   current full handshake cost). Existence => guest has bound.
2. Once the file appears, do the existing CONNECT/OK handshake one
   shot. The 5s read timeout still catches a guest that bound but
   never called accept().

The fallback-to-CONNECT/OK after stat returns is intentional: it
covers "bind succeeded but accept() not yet ready" without wedging
the probe. It is NOT premature complication.

## Brittleness contract

The companion-file naming is a Firecracker implementation detail, not
a stable API. The probe must:
- Document the exact Firecracker version range under which the naming
  was verified (in m80-vsock README under a new "Readiness contract"
  section).
- Keep CONNECT/OK as a hard fallback so a future Firecracker that
  changes the naming degrades to today's behavior, not failure.
- Re-verify on Firecracker upgrade as an explicit checklist item.

## Quick wins independent of this change

Tracked in m80-bgas (sibling): drop poll interval 500ms -> 100ms,
raise budget 30s -> 60s. m80-bgas should land first as a backstop.

## Acceptance (rolled-up)

- Leaf 1 verifies (or refutes) host-visible companion-file creation
  on a real KVM host under the in-tree Firecracker version.
- If verification passes: `phase_12b` uses the stat probe; CONNECT/OK
  becomes a one-shot post-stat handshake; latency from `InstanceStart`
  PUT to `Channel` returning `Ok` < 1s on idle host.
- m80-vsock README and m80-firecracker README updated to document the
  new readiness contract and its brittleness.
- Smoke test still passes; the simulated-load flake disappears or is
  documented as out-of-scope.

## Sibling beads

- m80-bgas (P2): the polling-constants-only quick win. Lands first.
- m80-6gv9 (P2): inotify upgrade. Stacks on top of m80-tv7i.
close_reason: premise-refuted: Firecracker creates `<uds>_<port>` only when GUEST initiates outbound (see firecracker muxer.rs:619-641). Host-side stat-poll on guest bind() is impossible. Empirical confirmed: 25s lifecycle observation showed only `vsock.sock` exists, no `vsock.sock_9001`. Verification: docs/verifications/m80-tv7i.1-vsock-companion-file.md. Pivot: m80-7tpy becomes primary readiness path (its mechanism is exactly what the source code supports — host pre-listens on `<uds>_<port>`, guest connects out).

title: VERIFY: probe whether Firecracker creates <vsock_uds>_<port> on guest bind()
description:
Gating leaf for m80-tv7i. Before any implementation work, verify on a
real KVM host that Firecracker creates a host-visible file at
`<vsock_uds>_<port>` when (and only when) m80-guestd executes
`VsockListener::bind((VMADDR_CID_ANY, 9001))`.

## Why this is the first leaf

Firecracker's documented vsock semantics describe `<uds>_<port>` as
the **host-side listener** for **guest-initiated** outbound
connections, not as an artifact of a guest bind. If verification
refutes the premise, the rest of m80-tv7i must be re-planned (likely
collapsing to m80-bgas + a future serial-console-watch leaf under
m80-6gv9 once `PUT /logger` is wired).

Do NOT skip this leaf. Do NOT start IMPL until this leaf is closed.

## Procedure

1. Boot the existing `end_to_end_real_kvm` test to a Running
   sandbox (or run `scripts/smoke.sh` once and pause it before
   `stop()` — easiest way to get a live VM).
2. Locate the host-side jail directory:
   `<run_root>/<vm_id>/firecracker/<vm_id>/root/`
3. Stat the candidate companion path:
   `<jail>/vsock.sock_9001`
4. Record three observations on a real KVM host running the
   in-tree Firecracker version:
   - Does the path exist after `InstanceStart` returns?
   - Does it exist after the guest has bound but before any host
     CONNECT/OK?
   - When in the boot sequence does it first appear (timestamp
     vs `InstanceStart` PUT)?
5. Cross-check against a guest variant that does NOT bind port 9001
   (temporarily comment out the bind in m80-guestd, rebuild rootfs,
   relaunch). If the file appears anyway, the file is unrelated to
   guest bind.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Manual run on KVM host produces a yes/no answer with timestamps,
      captured in a comment on this bead via `br update --notes`.
- [ ] If yes: the exact path format and creation timing are recorded
      (e.g., "appears within 5ms of guestd `bind()`; persists until
      VM stop"). This unblocks the IMPL leaf.
- [ ] If no: this bead is closed with `--reason "premise-refuted"`,
      the parent m80-tv7i is closed with the same reason, and a new
      bead is filed under m80-6gv9 to investigate the
      `PUT /logger`-based serial console watch as the next-best
      latency win.
- [ ] No code changes land from this leaf — observation only.

## Files / paths

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs` — `phase_12b_ready_probe`,
  `vsock_uds = jail.jail_path.join("vsock.sock")`
- `crates/m80-guestd/src/main.rs:57` — `VsockListener::bind_with_cid_port(VMADDR_CID_ANY, port)`
- `scripts/smoke.sh` — easy harness for getting a Running VM
- Firecracker upstream vsock doc:
  https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/main/docs/vsock.md

## Out of scope

- Writing a Rust integration test (see TEST-INT leaf).
- Touching `phase_12b_ready_probe`.
- Documenting the contract in READMEs (see DOCS leaf).

title: IMPL: stat-based two-phase ready probe in phase_12b
description:
Replace the polling loop in `phase_12b_ready_probe` with a two-phase
probe: stat the companion file, then do one CONNECT/OK handshake.

BLOCKED on m80-tv7i.1 (VERIFY) closing with a "yes" outcome.

## Today (crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:423)

- `READY_POLL_INTERVAL = 500ms`, `READY_TIMEOUT = 30s`
- Each loop iteration calls `Channel::open_uds_only` even when
  Firecracker has not yet seen guestd bind.

## After

- Phase A: stat `<vsock_uds_parent>/vsock.sock_<GUEST_PORT_DEFAULT>`
  at 10ms intervals until it exists, capped at the overall ready
  deadline.
- Phase B: a single `Channel::open_uds_only(vsock_uds, port)` call,
  reusing the existing 5s read timeout to catch a guest that bound
  but didn't `accept()`.
- New constants colocated with the existing ones:
  ```
  const STAT_POLL_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(10);
  ```
  Keep `READY_TIMEOUT` here — the budget is the parent's job; let
  m80-bgas own the 30s -> 60s change. No constants change here that
  m80-bgas also touches.
- The companion-port computation lives next to the probe (don't
  add a public `companion_path()` helper to m80-vsock yet — three
  near-identical lines beat a generic helper per CLAUDE.md).

## Fallback

If Phase A times out without the file appearing, fall back to a
single CONNECT/OK attempt before returning `VsockError::NotReady`.
Rationale: a future Firecracker that drops the companion file should
degrade to today's behavior, not fail outright. Document the
fallback as the brittleness escape hatch.

title: TEST-UNIT: fake companion-file appearance drives phase_12b stat phase
description:
Unit test that exercises the stat-phase loop without booting a real
VM. Validates: (a) probe returns once the file appears, (b) probe
times out cleanly when it never appears, (c) ordering — stat phase
runs before any UDS connect attempt.

BLOCKED on m80-tv7i.2 (IMPL) opening; this leaf can author tests in
parallel against the planned API but cannot land until IMPL lands.

## Strategy

The current `phase_12b_ready_probe` is a private `fn` in
`m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs`. Two options:

1. **Extract a small helper** `wait_for_companion_file(path, deadline,
   poll) -> Result<(), VsockError::NotReady>` next to the probe and
   `pub(crate)` it. Test it from
   `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/ready_probe_stat_phase.rs` with a
   thread that creates the file after a delay.

2. **Inline test in launch.rs** under `#[cfg(test)] mod tests {}`.

Pick option 1 — it keeps `launch.rs` under the 500-line guideline
and matches existing tests/ layout.

## Acceptance

- [ ] New file `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/ready_probe_stat_phase.rs`
      with three `#[test]`s, each scenario in its own fn (no bundled
      assertions per CLAUDE.md "What we don't want"):
      - `companion_file_present_at_start_returns_immediately`
      - `companion_file_appears_after_delay_returns_ok`
      - `companion_file_never_appears_returns_not_ready`
- [ ] No mocking of UDS connect — the helper under test only does
      the stat-phase work. Connect-phase coverage is owned by
      m80-vsock's existing `tests/handshake.rs`.
- [ ] Tests use `tempfile::tempdir()` and write the companion file
      via `std::fs::OpenOptions::create_new(true)` to mirror what
      Firecracker would do on bind.
- [ ] Tests run in well under 1 second total.

title: TEST-INT: real-KVM latency benchmark — InstanceStart -> Channel Ok < 1s
description:
Integration test that boots a real Firecracker VM and measures the
elapsed time from `InstanceAction::InstanceStart` PUT returning to
`phase_12b_ready_probe` returning `Ok(Channel)`. Pins the latency
target so a future regression (or a Firecracker version that drops
the companion file and forces fallback) is caught.

BLOCKED on m80-tv7i.2 (IMPL).

## Strategy

Extend `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/end_to_end_real_kvm.rs` with a
sibling `#[ignore]` test rather than touching the existing happy-path
test (the existing one stays a smoke; this one is a perf
characterization).

The test must:
- Run the same `Backend::new` + `admit` + `launch` path as the
  existing test.
- Capture an `Instant` immediately before `client.instance_action`
  and another immediately after `phase_12b_ready_probe` returns —
  this requires either (a) exposing the timing through a hook on
  `RunningSandbox`, (b) instrumenting the launch with `tracing` and
  parsing spans, or (c) duplicating the relevant phase calls in the
  test. Option (a) is cleanest: add a `pub fn ready_probe_elapsed
  (&self) -> Duration` on `RunningSandbox` measured during
  `launch()`. Option (c) is forbidden (couples test to internals).
- Assert `elapsed < Duration::from_secs(1)` on idle host.
- Run a small loop (5x) and assert P95 < 1s, not just min.

## Acceptance

- [ ] New test fn `ready_probe_under_one_second` in
      `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/end_to_end_real_kvm.rs`,

- "Idle host" is squishy. Document the host conditions assumed

title: Storage & Filesystem
description:
Purpose: per-VM rootfs cloning, scratch image hydration, post-stop change extraction (opt-in, generic — not gated on EffectClass).
Contract: clones isolated per VM; hydration opaque to guest; extraction post-stop only; admissibility scan rejects symlinks/specials; atomic swap with rollback on failure.
Surface: storage.rs (~992 LOC).
Evidence: m80/docs/behaviors/storage/ + m80/<crate>/tests/storage/.
notes: Update 2026-05-04 (post-storage-pivot): Sub-epic m80-urc.1 (per-VM rootfs cloning) is closed premise-refuted. The cloning behavior is replaced by shared-RO-base + per-VM-sparse-overlay; that work lives under m80-ovrl, not under m80-urc. m80-urc retains responsibility for scratch (workspace) image creation, hydration, and post-stop change extraction, which are unaffected by the rootfs pivot.

title: Per-VM rootfs cloning
description:
[CLOSED 2026-05-04 — PREMISE REFUTED]

Original premise: each VM gets a private byte-for-byte copy of the base ext4 under its run-dir. Refuted by direct measurement (727 ms storage_prep per launch, ~256 MiB working-set churn) and by docs/exploration/firecracker-shared-rootfs.md showing N-VM read-only sharing of the same host file is safe and explicitly supported by Firecracker.

Superseded by m80-ovrl: shared RO base file (single inode, page-cache deduplicated) + per-VM sparse ext4 overlay + in-guest overlayfs. The four sub-leaves (cloning, parent-dir creation, base-identity pre-clone verify, CopyRootfs error) are obsolete.

title: Drop-in config.d/ directory support for m80 config (deep TOML merge)
description:
Support /etc/m80/config.d/*.toml (and the user-config equivalent) with deep-table TOML merge applied in lexicographic order. Standard pattern in production runtimes.

## Reference

kata-exploration/10-dx-docs-config.md and src/libs/kata-types/src/config/drop_in.rs in kata (~384 LOC). Pattern: read base config; iterate config.d/ in lexicographic order; for each .toml file deep-merge into the running config (later wins on scalar conflicts, vectors replace). Silent on NotFound for the directory itself.

## Why

Ops wants to layer environment-specific overrides without touching base config. Single file forces edit-on-deploy; drop-ins compose cleanly.

## Scope

- Insert config.d/ layer between base and env vars in the precedence chain (per m80-v7t.2).
- Deep-table merge: nested tables merge recursively; scalars overwrite; arrays replace (don't concatenate).
- Lexicographic file order; document this so users can prefix with 10-, 20-, etc.
- Silent on missing directory; loud on parse error.
- m80 config show reflects the merged result.

## Acceptance

- Test: base config + two drop-ins (one overrides scalar, one adds nested table) produces expected merged output.
- m80-v7t README documents the precedence chain including config.d/.
- Lexicographic ordering pinned in a regression test (10-foo.toml vs 20-bar.toml).

title: m80-bench: --diff <baseline.json> for per-phase regression detection during perf iteration
description:
Make perf iteration cheap. cc2aed2 added per-phase timing instrumentation; the obvious next step is comparing two runs.

## Why

During a perf push (e.g. m80-rrp.3 snapshot work, m80-bgas poll cadence), the workflow is "change something, run bench, eyeball numbers, did it help?" Eyeballing two columns of timings is error-prone and slow. Tooling beats vigilance.

## Scope

- m80-bench --json emits per-phase timings as a structured document (uses the m80-bpuf envelope).
- m80-bench --diff <baseline.json> runs the bench, then prints a per-phase delta table: phase | baseline_p50 | new_p50 | delta_us | delta_pct, sorted by abs(delta_us) desc.
- Color the deltas (red regression, green improvement) when stdout is a tty.
- Threshold flag: --fail-on-regress=10pct exits non-zero if any phase regresses past threshold (CI-friendly).

## Out of scope

- Persistent benchmark database (just files).
- Cross-machine baseline normalization (compare same host).

## Acceptance

- m80-bench --json > a.json; (apply change); m80-bench --diff a.json shows the delta.
- --fail-on-regress threshold tested.
- README of bench script + scripts/bench.sh documents the workflow.
notes: Implemented 2026-05-05 in commit cdc46d9. scripts/bench-summary.py (791 LOC, 31 unittest cases) with compute/summarize/diff subcommands. bench-cold-launch.sh writes per-run CSVs to mktemp dir for clean compute input, auto-saves snapshot to benches/snapshots/<ts>.json with latest.json symlink. Envelope shape {version:1, data:...} matches m80-bpuf intent. --fail-on-regress for CI gating. ANSI-colored tty output. Stdlib only.
close_reason: implemented; commit cdc46d9 on main
